paras.en: Still, it would be difficult for Mr. Eisenkot, who ran on a center-right campaign, to form an alliance with the largest Arab party, the Joint List, whose leaders often harshly criticize Israel’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，对于以中右翼竞选的艾森科特来说，要与最大的阿拉伯政党“联合名单”结成联盟还是很困难的，该党的领导人经常严厉批评以色列在加沙和约旦河西岸的行动。

paras.en: At the salon in Jaffa, Ms. Katz’s hairdresser, Saado Zorob, 48, an Arab citizen, said that Jewish Israelis seemed happy to be treated by Arab physicians at hospitals and to eat at Arab restaurants but that many were unwilling to give Arab citizens a role in charting the country’s future.
paras.zh: 在雅法的沙龙里，卡茨女士的理发师、48 岁的阿拉伯公民萨多·佐罗布 (Saado Zorob) 表示，犹太以色列人似乎很高兴在医院接受阿拉伯医生的治疗，并在阿拉伯餐馆吃饭，但许多人不愿意让阿拉伯公民在规划国家未来方面发挥作用。

paras.en: “I feel like garbage,” he said as he was blow drying Ms. Katz’s hair. He added that he wished Mr. Eisenkot had the courage to form a government with the Arab caucus. Another election might benefit Mr. Netanyahu. “I’m worried that if the deadlock yields another round of elections, many Arabs will stay home,” he said
paras.zh: “我感觉自己像个垃圾，”他一边吹干卡茨女士的头发一边说道。他补充说，他希望艾森科特先生有勇气与阿拉伯核心小组一起组建政府。另一次选举可能会让内塔尼亚胡先生受益。 “我担心，如果僵局导致新一轮选举，许多阿拉伯人将呆在家里，”他说

paras.en: To many supporters of Mr. Netanyahu, a Jewish-Arab coalition would be a nightmare.
paras.zh: 对于内塔尼亚胡先生的许多支持者来说，犹太-阿拉伯联盟将是一场噩梦。

paras.en: Yakov Matzlawi, 51, a Likud member who manages a men’s undergarment stall in a market in Ramla, near Tel Aviv, said the mood among Netanyahu supporters he knew was subdued. Mr. Netanyahu didn’t lose, he said, but he didn’t win either, and many of on the right were still confused about what the results meant for the country.
paras.zh: 51 岁的利库德集团成员雅科夫·马茨拉维 (Yakov Matzlawi) 在特拉维夫附近的拉姆拉 (Ramla) 的一个市场上经营一个男士内衣摊位，他表示，据他所知，内塔尼亚胡支持者的情绪低迷。内塔尼亚胡先生没有输，他说，但他也没有赢，许多右翼人士仍然对结果对国家意味着什么感到困惑。

paras.en: “What’s important is that we remain in the game,” he said.
paras.zh: “重要的是我们要留在游戏中，”他说。

paras.en: Five miles south, in the city of Rehovot, Shira Barkan, 49, a therapist who wanted to see Mr. Netanyahu’s government fall, sat with her teenage daughter at an açai shop, their bowls only half eaten. “I don’t have much of an appetite,” she said.
paras.zh: 向南 5 英里的雷霍沃特市，49 岁的希拉·巴尔坎 (Shira Barkan) 是一名治疗师，她希望看到内塔尼亚胡政府垮台。她和十几岁的女儿坐在巴西莓店里，他们的碗只吃了一半。 “我没什么胃口，”她说。

paras.en: She had gone to bed the night before hopeful, she said, but “woke up in the morning with Bibi again,” using Mr. Netanyahu’s nickname. In her view, Mr. Netanyahu’s extremist government was leading Israel toward global isolation.
paras.zh: 她说，前一天晚上她满怀希望地入睡，但“早上又和比比一起醒来”，这是内塔尼亚胡先生的昵称。在她看来，内塔尼亚胡先生的极端主义政府正在带领以色列走向全球孤立。

paras.en: “Israelis are amazing people, and they deserve leadership that will not only protect us from external wrongs, but also stop its own wrongdoing,” she said.
paras.zh: 她说：“以色列人是了不起的人民，他们应该得到领导，这不仅能保护我们免受外部错误的侵害，还能制止其自身的错误行为。”

paras.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party is persisting with unproven allegations that Israel’s Arab voters have “stolen the elections.” Israel’s official elections committee has said there was no indication of widespread irregularities in the election on Tuesday. On Wednesday, the Likud again said that Arab parties — which are expected to receive a historically high number of parliamentary seats — had stolen the vote and called for the police and intelligence services to investigate.
paras.zh: 总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团坚持未经证实的指控，称以色列的阿拉伯选民“窃取了选举”。以色列官方选举委员会表示，没有迹象表明周二的选举存在广泛的违规行为。周三，利库德集团再次表示，预计将获得历史最高议会席位的阿拉伯政党窃取了选票，并呼吁警方和情报部门进行调查。

paras.en: Analysts say that Netanyahu is trying to de-legitimize votes by Arab citizens of Israel, fearing that his leading Jewish Israeli opponents might try to link up with the newly empowered Arab political bloc in an effort to unseat him.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，内塔尼亚胡正试图取消以色列阿拉伯公民投票的合法性，担心他的主要犹太以色列反对者可能会试图与新获得权力的阿拉伯政治集团联合起来，试图推翻他。

paras.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel fell short of outright victory on Tuesday night. But he has still emerged with a good chance of clinging to power.
paras.zh: 周二晚上，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡未能取得彻底胜利。但他仍然有很好的机会保住权力。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, 77, has plenty of political blessings to count after the vote. His Likud party is set to remain the largest in the Israeli Parliament, defying the pre-election polls. His rivals, led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot, secured far less support and have been left more divided than expected.
paras.zh: 77 岁的内塔尼亚胡在投票后获得了很多政治上的祝福。他领导的利库德集团将不顾选前民意调查，继续成为以色列议会中最大的政党。由前将军加迪·艾森科特领导的他的竞争对手获得的支持远远少于预期，而且分歧也比预期更大。

paras.en: Analysts say the result, with neither bloc securing enough votes to form a clear majority, could easily lead to weeks or months of political gridlock — a scenario that suits Mr. Netanyahu just fine. He will remain in charge as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed or new elections have to be held.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，结果是，两个阵营都无法获得足够的选票来形成绝对多数，很容易导致数周或数月的政治僵局——这种情况非常适合内塔尼亚胡先生。他将继续担任看守总理，直到新政府组建或必须举行新的选举。

paras.en: It is a remarkable turnaround for Mr. Netanyahu, whose critics blamed him for failing to prevent the Hamas-led attack on Oct. 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israeli history. A consummate political survivor of more than three decades in Israeli politics, Mr. Netanyahu is famous for out-negotiating and manipulating almost every opponent who has tried to end his rule.
paras.zh: 对于内塔尼亚胡先生来说，这是一个显着的转变，他的批评者指责他未能阻止哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日以色列历史上最致命的一天发生的袭击。内塔尼亚胡先生是以色列政坛三十多年的完美政治幸存者，以谈判和操纵几乎所有试图结束其统治的对手而闻名。

paras.en: “Netanyahu is still in the driver’s seat,” said Natan Sachs, an expert on Israeli politics at the Middle East Institute, a Washington-based research group. “He’s still in control of most events, and that’s where he likes to be.”
paras.zh: “内塔尼亚胡仍然占据主导地位，”华盛顿研究机构中东研究所的以色列政治专家纳坦·萨克斯说。 “他仍然控制着大多数事件，这就是他喜欢的地方。”

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, the longest serving prime minister in Israeli history, still has some headaches. The hard-line coalition he formed in 2022 — the most far-right in Israeli history — is set to lose its majority in Israel’s 120-member Parliament.
paras.zh: 以色列历史上任职时间最长的总理内塔尼亚胡仍然面临一些令人头痛的问题。他于 2022 年组建的强硬联盟——以色列历史上最右翼的联盟——将失去以色列 120 名议员议会中的多数席位。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu could also end up losing if Mr. Eisenkot, whose bloc trails the prime minister’s coalition by several seats, chooses to work with the Arab parties that performed better than ever to oust him.
paras.zh: 如果艾森科特选择与表现比以往任何时候都表现更好的阿拉伯政党合作推翻他，内塔尼亚胡最终也可能会失败。艾森科特的阵营落后于总理联盟几个席位。

paras.en: But Mr. Eisenkot is likely to struggle to form such an alliance, given how Israeli public opinion has shifted since the Oct. 7 attacks. Even though Arab leaders in Israel generally condemned the attacks, many Jewish Israelis still regard partnering with them as unacceptable.
paras.zh: 但考虑到自 10 月 7 日袭击以来以色列公众舆论的转变，艾森科特可能很难组建这样的联盟。尽管以色列的阿拉伯领导人普遍谴责这些袭击，但许多犹太以色列人仍然认为与他们合作是不可接受的。

paras.en: “Netanyahu knew he was going to have a weaker bloc. But he knew that his goal, even if he couldn’t get a 61-seat majority, would be to prevent his rivals from forming a government,” said Mazal Mualem, who has written a biography of Mr. Netanyahu. “And it seems he’s succeeded.”
paras.zh: “内塔尼亚胡知道他将拥有一个更弱的集团。但他知道，即使他无法获得 61 个席位的多数席位，他的目标也将是阻止他的竞争对手组建政府，”为内塔尼亚胡先生撰写传记的马扎尔·穆阿利姆 (Mazal Mualem) 说。 “看来他成功了。”

paras.en: All this was hard to imagine just three years ago. Mr. Netanyahu’s public standing plunged after the Oct. 7 attacks, when 1,200 in Israel were killed and 250 were taken hostage, igniting the war in Gaza. Even fervent supporters of the prime minister feared his time in office would end because of his failure to prevent the catastrophe.
paras.zh: 这一切在三年前还是难以想象的。 10 月 7 日的袭击导致以色列 1,200 人死亡、250 人被劫持为人质，并引发了加沙战争，内塔尼亚胡的公众形象一落千丈。即使是总理的狂热支持者也担心他的任期将因他未能阻止这场灾难而结束。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, however, has tenaciously clambered his way back without accepting any responsibility for the devastating security lapse. Instead, he blamed the assault on Israeli security chiefs, launched a series of military campaigns in Lebanon and Iran that killed some of Israel’s most significant foes, and ran his electoral campaign focused on amplifying fears of Israel’s Arab parties.
paras.zh: 然而，内塔尼亚胡先生顽强地爬回来，没有承担对这一毁灭性安全漏洞的任何责任。相反，他将此次袭击归咎于以色列安全负责人，在黎巴嫩和伊朗发起了一系列军事行动，杀死了以色列的一些最重要的敌人，并在竞选活动中强调了加剧对以色列阿拉伯政党的恐惧。

paras.en: On Tuesday, a swath of Jewish Israelis threw their support behind him, defying Mr. Netanyahu’s critics at home and abroad. The prime minister gave a fiery speech overnight on Wednesday as initial exit polls showed he had outperformed expectations vowing to establish “a patriotic, strong, right-wing government.”
paras.zh: 周二，大批犹太以色列人无视内塔尼亚胡国内外的批评者，支持他。周三晚上，总理发表了激烈的讲话，最初的出口民意调查显示，他的表现超出了预期，誓言要建立“一个爱国、强大的右翼政府”。

paras.en: While a slight shift in the results could upend the electoral map, Mr. Netanyahu has several options for how he might stay in power.
paras.zh: 虽然结果的轻微变化可能会颠覆选举版图，但内塔尼亚胡先生对于如何继续掌权有多种选择。

paras.en: One path would be to try to block any new government from being formed, forcing Israel to hold new elections. Mr. Netanyahu’s opponents — who threw years of energy and planning into the recent vote only to fall short — would struggle to do better in a new vote, analysts say.
paras.zh: 一种途径是试图阻止任何新政府的组建，迫使以色列举行新的选举。分析人士表示，内塔尼亚胡的反对者在最近的投票中投入了多年的精力和计划，但最终未能成功，他们将很难在新的投票中做得更好。

paras.en: “There’s a general sense that this was the opposition’s big chance,” Mr. Sachs said. “From Netanyahu’s perspective, he can throw the dice again and again.”
paras.zh: “人们普遍认为这是反对派的大好机会，”萨克斯说。 “从内塔尼亚胡的角度来看，他可以一次又一次地掷骰子。”

paras.en: Another option would be to form a unity government with one of his opponents. But that will be difficult as long as Mr. Netanyahu insists on staying in the prime minister’s office.
paras.zh: 另一种选择是与他的对手之一组建联合政府。但只要内塔尼亚胡坚持留在总理办公室，这就会很困难。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot has vowed not to serve under Mr. Netanyahu, although a national emergency — such as renewed fighting with Iran — could change that calculation.
paras.zh: 艾森科特发誓不会在内塔尼亚胡手下任职，尽管国家紧急状态——例如与伊朗重新爆发战斗——可能会改变这一想法。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu could also try to pick off potential right-wing defectors from Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc. These include opposition leaders who served in previous Netanyahu governments, such as Naftali Bennett, who leads the center-right Together party, and Avigdor Liberman, who leads the right-wing Yisrael Beitenu.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生还可以尝试从艾森科特先生的集团中剔除潜在的右翼叛逃者。其中包括曾在内塔尼亚胡前任政府任职的反对派领导人，例如领导中右翼团结党的纳夫塔利·贝内特和领导右翼以色列贝特努的阿维格多·利伯曼。

paras.en: Both men are right-wing supporters of Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Both refrained from explicitly endorsing Mr. Eisenkot, Mr. Netanyahu’s main challenger, as the opposition bloc’s candidate for prime minister.
paras.zh: 两人都是以色列占领的约旦河西岸犹太人定居点的右翼支持者。两人都没有明确支持内塔尼亚胡的主要挑战者艾森科特作为反对派集团的总理候选人。

paras.en: But rekindling their old partnerships with Mr. Netanyahu would be difficult. Both Mr. Bennett and Mr. Liberman have considerable bad blood with the prime minister. They have also been strident in demanding an independent commission of inquiry into the failures surrounding the Oct. 7 disaster, which Mr. Netanyahu has resisted.
paras.zh: 但重新点燃与内塔尼亚胡先生的旧有伙伴关系将是困难的。贝内特先生和利伯曼先生都与首相有很大的不和。他们还强烈要求成立一个独立委员会，对 10 月 7 日灾难的失败进行调查，但内塔尼亚胡先生对此表示抵制。

paras.en: Gadi Eisenkot, the leading figure in Israel’s political opposition, had hoped voters would deliver him a clear mandate to form a government, and begin a new era without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the helm.
paras.zh: 以色列政治反对派领袖加迪·艾森科特曾希望选民给予他组建政府的明确授权，并在没有总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡掌舵的情况下开启一个新时代。

paras.en: The initial results show, however, that Mr. Eisenkot and his allies have no easy path to power. They face a dilemma: To secure enough seats in parliament to form a government, they either need to cooperate with Arab-led parties — anathema to many Israelis — or join with Mr. Netanyahu or members of his right-wing alliance.
paras.zh: 然而，初步结果表明，艾森科特及其盟友的掌权之路并不平坦。他们面临着两难境地：为了在议会中获得足够的席位来组建政府，他们要么需要与阿拉伯领导的政党合作（这对许多以色列人来说是一种厌恶），要么与内塔尼亚胡先生或其右翼联盟成员合作。

paras.en: “He’s in a Catch-22,” said Shira Efron, chair of Israel policy at the RAND Corporation. “He doesn’t have a lot of great options.”
paras.zh: “他陷入了第二十二条军规，”兰德公司以色列政策主席希拉·埃夫隆(Shira Efron)说。 “他没有太多好的选择。”

paras.en: If Mr. Eisenkot and the opposition were to join forces with the Arab parties, the results so far suggest that they would need the support of both the major ones: the socially conservative Raam party and the Joint List, a coalition of three factions.
paras.zh: 如果艾森科特先生和反对派要与阿拉伯政党联手，迄今为止的结果表明，他们需要两个主要政党的支持：社会保守派拉姆党和三个派系联盟联合名单党。

paras.en: “After Oct. 7, Israeli society will not accept that,” said Shalom Yerushalmi, a veteran political writer at the news site Zman Yisrael, referring to the 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel. “There’s no chance.”
paras.zh: “10 月 7 日之后，以色列社会将不会接受这一点，”新闻网站 Zman Yisrael 的资深政治作家 Shalom Yerushalmi 表示，他指的是 2023 年哈马斯领导的对以色列南部的袭击。 “没有机会了。”

paras.en: Many Israelis are opposed to any government that would rely on parties that are not Zionist, and would not want those parties to influence security policies or foreign affairs. On the campaign trail, a number of opposition members pledged never to agree to such an arrangement.
paras.zh: 许多以色列人反对任何依赖非犹太复国主义政党的政府，也不希望这些政党影响安全政策或外交事务。在竞选过程中，一些反对派成员承诺永远不会同意这样的安排。

paras.en: Although Raam’s leader, Mansour Abbas, has taken positions more amenable to Zionist members of the opposition, including putting less emphasis on the Palestinian cause, the Joint List has refused to make similar compromises.
paras.zh: 尽管拉姆的领导人曼苏尔·阿巴斯采取了更适合反对派犹太复国主义成员的立场，包括减少对巴勒斯坦事业的重视，但联合名单拒绝做出类似的妥协。

paras.en: In the aftermath of Oct. 7, the leaders of the parties in the Joint List reacted in different ways. Ayman Odeh, who was the head of Hadash, referred to “Hamas’s murderous attack” in an opinion essay for The New York Times. Ahmad Tibi, the leader of Taal, said Arab citizens were against targeting civilians.
paras.zh: 10月7日事件发生后，联合名单各方领导人做出了不同反应。哈达什领导人艾曼·奥德在《纽约时报》的一篇评论文章中提到了“哈马斯的凶残袭击”。塔尔领导人艾哈迈德·提比表示，阿拉伯公民反对针对平民。

paras.en: Sami Abou Shahadeh, the chairman of Balad, said the attack was “an important, historic event in the military sense,” though he later condemned the attack after the Israeli Supreme Court discussed disqualifying him from running for parliament.
paras.zh: 巴拉德主席萨米·阿布·沙哈德表示，这次袭击是“军事意义上的一次重要的历史性事件”，不过在以色列最高法院讨论取消他竞选议会的资格后，他谴责了这次袭击。

paras.en: The prospect of Mr. Eisenkot setting up a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu or members of his bloc appears to be just as challenging. He made Mr. Netanyahu’s record a central theme of his campaign, saying the Israeli prime minister should “go home” and suggesting that he was unfit to lead the country.
paras.zh: 艾森科特与内塔尼亚胡或其集团成员建立联合政府的前景似乎同样具有挑战性。他将内塔尼亚胡的记录作为其竞选活动的中心主题，称以色列总理应该“回家”，并暗示他不适合领导这个国家。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot may be able to come to an agreement with Mr. Netanyahu that excludes some of the most extreme elements of the current Israeli coalition from government — such as the far-right cabinet members Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. But to do so would be to go back on a theme of his campaign.
paras.zh: 艾森科特或许能够与内塔尼亚胡达成协议，将当前以色列联盟中一些最极端的成员排除在政府之外，例如极右翼内阁成员伊塔马尔·本格维尔和贝扎莱尔·斯莫特里奇。但这样做就等于背离了他竞选的主题。

paras.en: “If he goes for a unity government, he would be destroying the whole narrative he has built,” Mr. Yerushalmi said.
paras.zh: “如果他支持联合政府，他就会毁掉他所建立的整个叙事，”耶鲁沙尔米先生说。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot could attempt to convince members of Mr. Netanyahu’s party, Likud, to defect to his side, but that seems unlikely because the long-serving Israeli leader has in the past been highly effective at holding his coalition together.
paras.zh: 艾森科特可能会试图说服内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团成员倒戈到他一边，但这似乎不太可能，因为这位长期任职的以色列领导人过去在维系联盟方面非常有效。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition also includes some ultra-Orthodox parties, which Mr. Eisenkot could try to bring into his bloc. Yet many opposition members are at odds with lawmakers from those parties over the exemptions from military service that many ultra-Orthodox Israelis enjoy.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡的联盟还包括一些极端正统政党，艾森科特可以尝试将这些政党纳入自己的阵营。然而，许多反对派成员与这些政党的立法者在许多极端正统以色列人享有的兵役豁免问题上存在分歧。

paras.en: Another option for Mr. Eisenkot and his partners is to hold out for a new round of elections in the hope of achieving a more favorable result. But that scenario, analysts said, was fraught with pitfalls — Mr. Eisenkot’s supporters, including those living abroad, may be feel less motivated to show up to vote again.
paras.zh: 艾森科特及其伙伴的另一个选择是坚持举行新一轮选举，以期取得更有利的结果。但分析人士表示，这种情况充满了陷阱——艾森科特的支持者，包括那些居住在国外的人，可能会觉得没有动力再次去投票。

paras.en: More than 80 percent of votes have been counted. The initial results continue to suggest that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s alliance nor a bloc of opposition parties led by Gadi Eisenkot is likely to have gained enough seats to form the next government.
paras.zh: 超过80%的选票已经清点完毕。初步结果继续表明，无论是总理内塔尼亚胡的联盟还是加迪·艾森科特领导的反对党集团都不太可能获得足够的席位来组建下一届政府。

paras.en: The results of Israel’s pivotal parliamentary election will not be finalized at least until Thursday and it could be weeks until it is clear what kind of government will be formed and who will lead it. But some conclusions are already inescapable.
paras.zh: 以色列关键的议会选举的结果至少要到周四才能最终确定，可能需要几周时间才能明确将组建什么样的政府以及由谁来领导。但有些结论已经是不可避免的了。

paras.en: Arab citizens of Israel turned out to vote in record numbers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party gobbled up many votes that his right-wing and Orthodox Jewish coalition partners had expected would be theirs. And the pre-election polls failed to anticipate both phenomena.
paras.zh: 以色列的阿拉伯公民参加投票的人数创历史新高。总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团夺取了许多选票，而他的右翼和正统犹太联盟伙伴原以为这些选票会属于他们。选举前的民意调查未能预见到这两种现象。

paras.en: Much could still change. But with most of the votes counted by Wednesday afternoon, here are some initial takeaways.
paras.zh: 很多事情仍然可能发生变化。但由于大部分选票已在周三下午清点完毕，以下是一些初步结论。

paras.en: Netanyahu didn’t win, but Eisenkot lost.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡没有获胜，但艾森科特输了。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition appears to have shrunk considerably from the 64 parliamentary seats that it won in 2022: The latest results show it with around 54, well short of a majority in the 120-member Knesset, or Parliament. But he could wind up in better position to form a government than his chief rival, Gadi Eisenkot.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生的联盟似乎比 2022 年赢得的 64 个议会席位大幅缩减：最新结果显示，该联盟拥有约 54 个席位，远低于在 120 名议员的议会中获得多数席位。但他最终可能比他的主要竞争对手加迪·艾森科特更有能力组建政府。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief of staff, had two goals in the election: to lead the Jewish opposition parties to an outright majority or at least get very close to one, and to make sure his own party, Yashar, got more votes than any other. He failed on both counts, the initial results indicate.
paras.zh: 以色列前军事参谋长艾森科特在选举中有两个目标：带领犹太反对党获得绝对多数或至少非常接近多数，并确保他自己的政党“亚沙尔”获得比其他政党更多的选票。初步结果表明，他在这两方面都失败了。

paras.en: Reuven Hazan, a political science professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said that it had been hard to imagine better conditions for Mr. Eisenkot’s alliance ahead of the election. Mr. Netanyahu and his coalition were weighed down by anger over the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023 attacks and their failure to do more to free Israeli hostages; by anger over ultra-Orthodox Jewish draft-dodging in wartime; and by outrage over the government’s efforts to neuter the judiciary and allow growing settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, he said.
paras.zh: 耶路撒冷希伯来大学政治学教授鲁文·哈赞 (Reuven Hazan) 表示，很难想象选举前艾森科特的联盟会有更好的条件。内塔尼亚胡先生和他的联盟对哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日袭击以及他们未能采取更多行动解救以色列人质感到愤怒；对战时极端正统犹太人逃避兵役的愤怒；他说，政府试图压制司法机构，并允许定居者在以色列占领的约旦河西岸针对巴勒斯坦人实施越来越多的暴力行为，这引起了人们的愤怒。

paras.en: “The anti-Netanyahu camp had an election handed to them on a silver platter, and they still lost,” Mr. Hazan said. “Israelis have sent an ambiguous message: ‘We don’t really like the current government, but we don’t see a viable alternative.’”
paras.zh: “反内塔尼亚胡阵营已经把选举交给了他们，但他们仍然失败了，”哈赞先生说。 “以色列人发出了一个模棱两可的信息：‘我们并不真正喜欢现任政府，但我们看不到可行的替代方案。’”

paras.en: Netanyahu’s coalition shrank, but he has options.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡的联盟缩小了，但他有选择。

paras.en: As votes were being counted on Wednesday afternoon, Likud was poised to be the largest party in the larger of the two blocs of Jewish-led parties, meaning Mr. Netanyahu could well be given the chance to form a government, Mr. Hazan said.
paras.zh: 哈赞表示，周三下午计票时，利库德集团有望成为犹太人领导的两个政党集团中最大的政党，这意味着内塔尼亚胡很可能有机会组建政府。

paras.en: The long-serving Israeli premier may try to peel away some of Mr. Eisenkot’s putative partners in order to achieve a majority of 61 seats in Parliament. A number of them are as right-wing as he is, though all have more or less ruled out entering a Netanyahu-led government.
paras.zh: 这位长期任职的以色列总理可能会试图剥离艾森科特先生的一些假定合作伙伴，以在议会中获得 61 个席位的多数席位。他们中的一些人和他一样是右翼分子，尽管他们都或多或少地排除了加入内塔尼亚胡领导的政府的可能性。

paras.en: He could also try to form a national unity government with Mr. Eisenkot — perhaps with the assistance of President Trump, who has praised Mr. Netanyahu as a “warrior prime minister” and has made clear he wants Israel to join the United States in another round of war against Iran.
paras.zh: 他还可能尝试与艾森科特组建民族团结政府——也许会得到特朗普总统的协助。特朗普称赞内塔尼亚胡是“战士总理”，并明确表示希望以色列加入美国对伊朗的另一轮战争。

paras.en: Perhaps the most mind-bending option available to Mr. Netanyahu, given that he ran a scaremongering campaign that demonized Arab lawmakers and stoked fears of Arab voter turnout, would be to recruit an Arab party to join him in a government. He nearly did so once before, in 2022.
paras.zh: 鉴于内塔尼亚胡先生发起了一场妖魔化阿拉伯立法者并引发了对阿拉伯选民投票率的担忧的危言耸听活动，也许内塔尼亚胡先生可以采取的最令人费解的选择就是招募一个阿拉伯政党加入他的政府。此前，也就是 2022 年，他差点就做到了这一点。

paras.en: “It could very well be that they become indispensable,” said Dahlia Scheindlin, a pollster and political analyst, said of Arab lawmakers. “And Netanyahu has certainly demonstrated his willingness to do anything to stay in power.”
paras.zh: “他们很可能变得不可或缺，”民调专家兼政治分析师达丽娅·谢恩德林 (Dahlia Scheindlin) 在谈到阿拉伯立法者时说道。 “内塔尼亚胡无疑已经表明，他愿意不惜一切代价继续掌权。”

paras.en: Speaking of Jewish opposition parties in isolation ignores the fact that, when Arab parties are included, Mr. Netanyahu’s rivals appeared headed toward a significant majority in Parliament, with about 66 seats to roughly 54 for the prime minister’s bloc.
paras.zh: 孤立地谈论犹太反对党忽略了这样一个事实：如果将阿拉伯政党也包括在内，内塔尼亚胡的竞争对手似乎将在议会中占据绝大多数席位，总理集团将获得约 66 个席位，而总理集团则将获得约 54 个席位。

paras.en: “There is no need to go with the racist assumption that you need not count the Arabs,” said Gayil Talshir, a political scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem who is advising the opposition.
paras.zh: 为反对派提供咨询的耶路撒冷希伯来大学政治学家盖伊尔·塔尔希尔 (Gayil Talshir) 表示：“没有必要接受种族主义假设，即不需要计算阿拉伯人。”

paras.en: That means the Knesset in effect will be controlled by the anti-Netanyahu opposition, regardless of who ends up being prime minister. If the vote breakdown roughly holds, Ms. Talshir said she expected Mr. Eisenkot and his Jewish and Arab allies to elect a new parliamentary speaker, begin repealing unpopular laws and at least try to form a government — perhaps including some combination of Arab and ultra-Orthodox lawmakers.
paras.zh: 这意味着无论谁最终成为总理，以色列议会实际上都将由反内塔尼亚胡反对派控制。塔尔希尔表示，如果投票结果大致成立，她预计艾森科特和他的犹太和阿拉伯盟友将选出一位新的议长，开始废除不受欢迎的法律，并至少尝试组建一个政府——或许包括一些阿拉伯和极端正统派议员的组合。

paras.en: “I’m not saying it’s a good scenario to take the Knesset and not be able to form the government,” Ms. Talshir said. “It’s a disaster. But this is the hand they’re dealt, and they have to play it.”
paras.zh: 塔尔希尔女士说：“我并不是说拿下议会但无法组建政府是一个好的情况。” “这是一场灾难。但这就是他们面临的局面，他们必须打好它。”

paras.en: Arab voters broke records but could face rejection.
paras.zh: 阿拉伯选民打破了记录，但可能面临拒绝。

paras.en: Tuesday’s election appears to have had many losers. Mr. Netanyahu’s support shrank and Mr. Eisenkot came up short of his goal. The ultra-Orthodox parties were projected to lose seats, according to the latest returns, and two right-wing nationalist parties failed to make gains, despite four years in which they drove the Netanyahu government’s extreme policies in the West Bank.
paras.zh: 周二的选举似乎有很多失败者。内塔尼亚胡的支持率下降，艾森科特也未能实现他的目标。根据最新的民意调查结果，极端正统派政党预计将失去席位，而两个右翼民族主义政党尽管四年来推动内塔尼亚胡政府在西岸推行极端政策，但未能取得席位。

paras.en: The biggest ostensible winners were the Arab voters who voted in record numbers. But they could well wind up the most disappointed citizens of all, if the Jewish opposition leaders prove unwilling or unable to form a majority in an alliance with the Arab parties.
paras.zh: 表面上最大的赢家是投票人数创纪录的阿拉伯选民。但如果犹太反对派领导人不愿意或无法在与阿拉伯政党的联盟中获得多数席位，他们很可能会成为最失望的公民。

paras.en: “They’re saying, ‘We believe in Israeli democracy, we believe in the system, we want to be part of the system, and we want to be treated better,’” Mr. Hazan said. “And if Netanyahu forms a government, they’ll get none of that.”
paras.zh: “他们说，‘我们相信以色列的民主，我们相信这个制度，我们希望成为这个制度的一部分，我们希望得到更好的待遇，’”哈赞先生说。 “如果内塔尼亚胡组建政府，他们将一无所获。”

paras.en: Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, said he would not begin consulting party leaders about forming a government before next week, when he expects to receive the full official vote count. As head of state, Herzog will pick whoever he thinks has the best shot at assembling a majority in Parliament. If the first effort fails, he can ask up to two other candidates. If they also fail, new elections will be held. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said.
paras.zh: 以色列总统艾萨克·赫尔佐格表示，他不会在下周之前开始就组建政府问题与党派领导人进行磋商，预计届时将收到完整的官方计票结果。作为国家元首，赫尔佐格将挑选他认为最有可能在议会中获得多数席位的人。如果第一次尝试失败，他可以询问最多两名其他候选人。如果他们也失败，将举行新的选举。赫尔佐格说：“我们必须尽一切努力，尤其是在昨天之后，以避免另一轮选举。”

paras.en: Yakov Matzlawi, 51, who manages a men’s undergarment stall in the market in Ramla, a city near Tel Aviv, is an activist for Likud, Benjamin Netanyahu’s party. He said the right-wing voters he knows, including some critical of the prime minister and his government, were mobilized out of anxiety that the Israeli left and Arab parties would take power.
paras.zh: 51 岁的雅科夫·马茨拉维 (Yakov Matzlawi) 在特拉维夫附近城市拉姆拉的市场上经营着一个男士内衣摊位，他是本雅明·内塔尼亚胡 (Benjamin Netanyahu) 政党利库德集团 (Likud) 的积极分子。他说，他认识的右翼选民，包括一些批评总理及其政府的人，是出于对以色列左翼和阿拉伯政党掌权的焦虑而被动员起来的。

paras.en: “People voted against the Muslims and the secular Jews,” he said.
paras.zh: “人们投票反对穆斯林和世俗犹太人，”他说。

paras.en: Accountability for the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks has been a major election issue. Many residents of the communities hit hardest by the assault said they are disappointed that many Israelis had voted to return to office Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power at the time.
paras.zh: 追究哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日袭击事件的责任一直是选举的一个重大问题。受袭击影响最严重的社区的许多居民表示，他们对许多以色列人投票支持当时执政的本杰明·内塔尼亚胡总理重返办公室感到失望。

paras.en: Nili Bar Sinai, 76, a retired social worker whose husband was killed by militants in Be’eri, a kibbutz near the Gaza border, said that she hoped opposition leaders would have the “courage to join hands with the Arab parties,” a move that could unseat Netanyahu.
paras.zh: 76 岁的退休社会工作者尼利·巴尔·西奈 (Nili Bar Sinai) 的丈夫在加沙边境附近的基布兹贝埃里 (Be’eri) 被武装分子杀害。她说，她希望反对派领导人有“勇气与阿拉伯政党联手”，此举可能会让内塔尼亚胡下台。

paras.en: For many Israelis, Tuesday’s election represents a pivotal moment for the future of their country. For Israel’s neighbors in the Middle East, the stakes look decidedly different.
paras.zh: 对于许多以色列人来说，周二的选举代表着他们国家未来的关键时刻。对于以色列的中东邻国来说，利害关系看起来截然不同。

paras.en: Few expect the election — whoever ultimately emerges as the winner — to be a turning point for the region, or to fundamentally change Israel’s security doctrine, analysts say. That doctrine, which has hardened since the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, includes crippling the Iranian government, occupying areas of Lebanon and Syria, and often favoring military force over diplomacy.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，很少有人预计这次选举——无论谁最终获胜——将成为该地区的转折点，或者从根本上改变以色列的安全学说。自 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯领导的对以色列的袭击以来，这一学说变得更加坚定，包括削弱伊朗政府、占领黎巴嫩和叙利亚地区，以及往往倾向于军事力量而非外交。

paras.en: While the outcome of the election is unlikely to prompt Israel to change course, it may decide how far the country is prepared to take its regional ambitions.
paras.zh: 虽然选举结果不太可能促使以色列改变路线，但它可能决定该国准备在多大程度上实现其地区野心。

paras.en: Re-election for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, backed by his far-right coalition partners, could embolden him to again escalate the war with Iran and push diplomacy with Israel’s neighbors farther out of reach, analysts said.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，在极右翼联盟伙伴的支持下，本杰明·内塔尼亚胡总理连任可能会鼓励他再次升级与伊朗的战争，并使与以色列邻国的外交更加遥不可及。

paras.en: And in both Lebanon and Syria, where Israeli forces have established and expanded military-controlled buffer zones over the past two years, a win for Mr. Netanyahu could see Israel further entrench or expand its occupation.
paras.zh: 在过去两年里，以色列军队在黎巴嫩和叙利亚建立并扩大了军事控制的缓冲区，内塔尼亚胡的胜利可能会导致以色列进一步巩固或扩大其占领。

paras.en: Even if Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition doesn’t win, many in the region do not see “any major visible strategic difference among the candidates,” said Paul Salem, a nonresident senior associate at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
paras.zh: 战略与国际研究中心非常驻高级研究员保罗·塞勒姆表示，即使内塔尼亚胡先生的联盟没有获胜，该地区许多人也没有看到“候选人之间存在任何重大、明显的战略差异”。

paras.en: “They don’t see much difference in Israel’s forward defense that it insists on having — the occupied zones in Syria, in Lebanon, in Gaza and the West Bank that is just adding instability regionally,” he added.
paras.zh: 他补充说：“他们认为以色列坚持的前沿防御没有太大区别——叙利亚、黎巴嫩、加沙和约旦河西岸的占领区只会加剧地区不稳定。”

paras.en: The same is true of Palestinian statehood, which remains a distant prospect regardless of the election’s outcome. It has been a central issue for Israel’s neighbors and for American-led efforts to seek normalized relations between Israel and Gulf countries.
paras.zh: 巴勒斯坦建国也是如此，无论选举结果如何，巴勒斯坦建国仍然是一个遥远的前景。对于以色列的邻国以及以美国为首的寻求以色列与海湾国家关系正常化的努力来说，这一直是一个核心问题。

paras.en: Saudi Arabia and others have said any agreement with Israel would require the creation of a Palestinian state. But with Israeli proponents of a two-state solution now relegated to the political fringes, such a deal appears more distant than ever.
paras.zh: 沙特阿拉伯和其他国家表示，与以色列达成的任何协议都需要建立巴勒斯坦国。但由于以色列两国解决方案的支持者现在已被置于政治边缘，这样的协议似乎比以往任何时候都更加遥远。

paras.en: In Iran, the outcome of the Israeli election could have more immediate consequence. While Israel’s animosity toward Tehran is unlikely to change regardless of who is in power, a change in leadership could alter the course of the war.
paras.zh: 在伊朗，以色列选举的结果可能会产生更直接的后果。尽管无论谁掌权，以色列对德黑兰的敌意都不太可能改变，但领导层的更迭可能会改变战争的进程。

paras.en: Ahead of the election, Mr. Netanyahu sought to energize his voter base by saying that he was the person President Trump wanted by his side to “finish the job once and for all.”
paras.zh: 选举前，内塔尼亚胡先生试图激励他的选民基础，他说他是特朗普总统希望在他身边“一劳永逸地完成任务”的人。

paras.en: Iranian officials believe a victory for Mr. Netanyahu could prolong the American-Israeli military campaign against Iran, leading to an even more protracted conflict, analysts say. And there is no clear sign among the opposition that they would seek to curtail Israel’s confrontation with Iran.
paras.zh: 分析人士称，伊朗官员认为，内塔尼亚胡的胜利可能会延长美国和以色列针对伊朗的军事行动，从而导致冲突更加旷日持久。反对派也没有明确迹象表明他们会寻求遏制以色列与伊朗的对抗。

paras.en: Israel’s current approach to Iran “poses a major threat to Iran’s security and very existence,” said Hadi Borhani, a professor of Israeli studies at the University of Tehran. “From this perspective, Netanyahu’s re-election poses a threat to Iran’s territorial integrity as a whole.”
paras.zh: 德黑兰大学以色列研究教授哈迪·博尔哈尼表示，以色列目前对伊朗的态度“对伊朗的安全和生存构成了重大威胁”。 “从这个角度来看，内塔尼亚胡的连任对伊朗的整体领土完整构成了威胁。”

paras.en: It’s nearly 8 a.m. in Israel and the outcome of Tuesday’s election is still unclear. More than 40 percent of the votes have been counted, according to the authorities, and most of the remaining ballots will be tallied within the next several hours. Then, officials will begin counting hundreds of thousands of ballots from Israeli soldiers, diplomats abroad and a few other categories of voters. That could take until Thursday.
paras.zh: 现在以色列已近上午 8 点，周二的选举结果仍不明朗。据当局称，超过 40% 的选票已经清点完毕，其余大部分选票将在接下来的几个小时内清点。然后，官员们将开始清点来自以色列士兵、驻外外交官和其他几类选民的数十万张选票。这可能需要到周四。

paras.en: Isaac Herzog, Israel’s president, has a largely ceremonial role — except after national elections, when it is his responsibility to choose a potential prime minister and then tasks that person with trying to form a government.
paras.zh: 以色列总统艾萨克·赫尔佐格(Isaac Herzog)在很大程度上扮演着仪式性的角色——全国选举之后除外，届时他有责任选择一位潜在的总理，然后责成该人组建政府。

paras.en: Since Israelis vote for a party or parties rather than an individual, the person who might lead the country is selected after the ballots are counted and parliamentary seats are allocated to parties according to their proportion of the vote. The president — who is separately elected by the Knesset, Israel’s single-chamber legislature — then convenes party leaders to hear their recommendations for prime minister before choosing someone to form a government.
paras.zh: 由于以色列人投票支持一个或多个政党而不是个人，因此可能领导国家的人是在计票后选出的，议会席位根据政党的得票比例分配给政党。总统由以色列单院立法机构以色列议会单独选举产生，然后召集各党派领导人听取他们对总理的建议，然后再选择某人组建政府。

paras.en: While the president can choose the leader of the party that won the most votes, he can also select another leader who seems more likely to assemble a coalition that can secure a vote of confidence in the Knesset.
paras.zh: 虽然总统可以选择赢得最多选票的政党的领导人，但他也可以选择另一位似乎更有可能组建联盟以确保议会获得信任票的领导人。

paras.en: In 2009, President Shimon Peres chose Benjamin Netanyahu — the current prime minister — even though his right-wing Likud party had won fewer votes than the centrist Kadima party.
paras.zh: 2009年，西蒙·佩雷斯总统选择了现任总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，尽管他的右翼利库德集团赢得的选票少于中间派前进党。

paras.en: Early exit polls on Wednesday suggest a tight race between the far-right coalition led by Mr. Netanyahu and the center-right opposition bloc that has called for change. The opposition bloc includes the Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot. But Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party appears to have received the most votes, which means he will argue that he should be selected as prime minister.
paras.zh: 周三早期的出口民意调查显示，内塔尼亚胡领导的极右翼联盟与呼吁变革的中右翼反对派集团之间存在着激烈的竞争。反对派集团包括加迪·艾森科特领导的亚沙尔党。但内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团似乎获得了最多的选票，这意味着他将主张自己应该被选为总理。

paras.en: Mr. Herzog, whose job is to stay above the political fray, is expected to face a difficult decision. He must discern whether the votes show that the majority of Israelis demanded change or if they indicated a preference for another Netanyahu government.
paras.zh: 赫尔佐格的工作是远离政治纷争，预计他将面临一个艰难的决定。他必须辨别投票是否表明大多数以色列人要求变革，或者是否表明他们倾向于另一个内塔尼亚胡政府。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu’s governing coalition, the most right-wing in Israel’s history, has drawn international condemnation, heightened tensions with allies and divided Israelis. Mr. Herzog has repeatedly criticized what he has called “a terrible process of brutalization” creeping into Israeli society, citing violence by Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank against Palestinians and the abuse of detainees in Israeli custody, which some far-right ministers in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition are accused of encouraging.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生的执政联盟是以色列历史上最右翼的联盟，它引起了国际社会的谴责，加剧了与盟友的紧张关系，并导致以色列人分裂。赫尔佐格多次批评他所称的“可怕的残酷过程”正在渗透到以色列社会，他列举了被占领的约旦河西岸犹太定居者对巴勒斯坦人的暴力行为，以及虐待以色列拘留中的被拘留者的行为，内塔尼亚胡联盟中的一些极右翼部长被指控鼓励这些行为。

paras.en: The Israeli president, who can grant criminal pardons and commute sentences, has also faced pressure from President Trump, who has called on him to pardon Mr. Netanyahu as he stands trial on corruption charges. Mr. Herzog has respectfully resisted, saying that “Israel is a sovereign state governed by the rule of law.”
paras.zh: 这位可以给予刑事赦免和减刑的以色列总统也面临着来自特朗普总统的压力，特朗普呼吁他在内塔尼亚胡因腐败指控受审时赦免他。赫尔佐格先生恭敬地予以抵制，称“以色列是一个法治的主权国家。”

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu has long resisted calls for an independent commission of inquiry into the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel that set off a devastating war in Gaza. He has also refused to take responsibility for any failures that led to the attack, angering many Israelis.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生长期以来一直拒绝成立独立调查委员会，调查 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯领导的对以色列的袭击，这场袭击在加沙引发了一场毁灭性的战争。他还拒绝对导致袭击的任何失误承担责任，这激怒了许多以色列人。

paras.en: But if the president taps Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief whose son was killed in the war in Gaza and who has vowed to launch a state inquiry into the 2023 attack, there is no guarantee he will succeed in forming a government. The center-right opposition bloc would need to ally with the country’s Arab parties, which appear to have secured more parliamentary seats than ever before. The bloc’s leaders have not agreed to such an alliance, while Mr. Netanyahu has effectively ruled out including Arab parties in a governing coalition.
paras.zh: 但如果总统任命艾森科特先生为代表，他的儿子在加沙战争中丧生，并誓言要对 2023 年的袭击事件展开国家调查，那么并不能保证他能成功组建政府。中右翼反对派集团需要与该国的阿拉伯政党结盟，这些政党似乎获得了比以往更多的议会席位。该集团领导人尚未同意建立这样的联盟，而内塔尼亚胡先生实际上已经排除了将阿拉伯政党纳入执政联盟的可能性。

paras.en: Both the far-right and far-left blocs face obstacles to assembling a governing majority. They would need agreements with other parties and factions that may be politically unpalatable, or even impossible.
paras.zh: 极右翼和极左翼集团在组建执政多数方面都面临障碍。他们需要与其他政党和派系达成协议，而这在政治上可能令人不快，甚至是不可能的。

paras.en: One of the most striking results from the election in Israel on Tuesday was the unusually strong showing by two leading Arab parties, whose voters turned out in record numbers to express their opposition to the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
paras.zh: 周二以色列选举中最引人注目的结果之一是两个主要阿拉伯政党异常强劲的表现，这两个政党的选民数量创纪录地表达了对本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理政府的反对。

paras.en: The final results have not been announced, but a range of exit polls conducted by Israeli broadcasters suggest that two of the parties — the socially conservative United Arab List, or Raam, and the left-wing Joint List — may have won a historically large number of seats in parliament and an important role in the formation of the country’s next government.
paras.zh: 最终结果尚未公布，但以色列广播公司进行的一系列出口民意调查显示，其中两个政党——社会保守的阿拉伯联合名单党（Raam）和左翼联合名单党——可能赢得了历史上数量最多的议会席位，并在该国下一届政府的组建中发挥了重要作用。

paras.en: Mansour Abbas, the leader of Raam, told a television interviewer that the turnout showed that Arab voters, who make up about 20 percent of Israel’s population, had channeled their “frustration and despair” into “hope.”
paras.zh: 拉姆领导人曼苏尔·阿巴斯对电视采访者表示，投票率表明，占以色列人口约 20% 的阿拉伯选民已将“沮丧和绝望”转化为“希望”。

paras.en: He said he wanted to replace Mr. Netanyahu’s government “in every possible way” and that his first priority was to “ensure that there is a chance of forming a government” that achieved that goal.
paras.zh: 他说，他希望“以一切可能的方式”取代内塔尼亚胡先生的政府，而他的首要任务是“确保有机会组建一个政府”来实现这一目标。

paras.en: The Arab parties’ strong showing may make them kingmakers. But building a governing coalition with Arab participation remains a fraught exercise in Israel. Many Israeli Jews believe that a parliamentary majority should not rely on the support of Arab lawmakers.
paras.zh: 阿拉伯政党的强劲表现可能会让他们成为国王的拥护者。但在以色列建立一个有阿拉伯人参与的执政联盟仍然是一项充满挑战的工作。许多以色列犹太人认为，议会多数不应依赖阿拉伯立法者的支持。

paras.en: Most Arab citizens are the descendants of Palestinians who remained in their homes during the 1948 Arab-Israel war at the time of Israel’s independence.
paras.zh: 大多数阿拉伯公民是巴勒斯坦人的后裔，他们在 1948 年阿以战争期间以色列独立时仍留在家乡。

paras.en: Today, they mostly live in separate towns from Jewish Israelis and face violence and discriminatory housing policies.
paras.zh: 如今，他们大多居住在与犹太以色列人不同的城镇，面临暴力和歧视性住房政策。

paras.en: Over the decades, disagreements, including over Israel’s nature as a Jewish state, have led many Arab voters to avoid the ballot box.
paras.zh: 几十年来，包括以色列作为犹太国家性质在内的分歧导致许多阿拉伯选民避开投票箱。

paras.en: This week, many Arab voters said they were furious at Mr. Netanyahu for his treatment of the Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza and for policies that they feel treat Palestinians in Israel as second-class citizens. Indeed, throughout the campaign, Mr. Netanyahu made overt appeals to anti-Arab prejudice.
paras.zh: 本周，许多阿拉伯选民表示，他们对内塔尼亚胡对待约旦河西岸和加沙巴勒斯坦人的方式以及他们认为将以色列境内的巴勒斯坦人视为二等公民的政策感到愤怒。事实上，在整个竞选过程中，内塔尼亚胡先生公开呼吁反阿拉伯偏见。

paras.en: “I’m very optimistic because people understand that this isn’t like ordinary elections — we want change,” said Kholoud Al-Zeinati, 39, an Arab Israeli voter who cast her ballot on Tuesday in the mixed Jewish-Arab city of Lod, where long lines formed at polling places. “Because we, as the Arab community, are the community that pays the biggest price across so many aspects of life, it’s important to come out and take part.”
paras.zh: “我非常乐观，因为人们知道这与普通选举不同，我们想要改变，”39 岁的阿拉伯裔以色列选民霍鲁德·阿尔泽纳蒂 (Kholoud Al-Zeinati) 说，她于周二在犹太裔阿拉伯人混居的罗德市投票，那里的投票点排起了长队。 “因为我们作为阿拉伯社区，是在生活的许多方面付出最大代价的社区，所以站出来参与进来很重要。”

paras.en: “I expect our votes to be truly decisive in shaping the next government and making things better for all of us,” she added.
paras.zh: 她补充说：“我希望我们的选票对于塑造下一届政府和让我们所有人的生活变得更好方面具有真正决定性的作用。”

paras.en: Of the two Arab parties that did well on Tuesday, only Raam has joined a coalition government in the past. That happened in 2021, when it joined the short-lived anti-Netanyahu coalition of Prime Minister Naftali Bennett.
paras.zh: 在周二表现出色的两个阿拉伯政党中，只有拉姆过去曾加入过联合政府。这发生在 2021 年，当时它加入了总理纳夫塔利·贝内特领导的短暂的反内塔尼亚胡联盟。

paras.en: Raam’s participation in that government outraged many right-wing Jewish voters, and when it collapsed after roughly one year, they backed Mr. Netanyahu, who went on to form the most hard-line government in Israel’s history.
paras.zh: 拉姆参与该政府激怒了许多右翼犹太选民，大约一年后该政府垮台时，他们支持了内塔尼亚胡，内塔尼亚胡后来组建了以色列历史上最强硬的政府。

paras.en: That government now faces the possibility that it may be brought down by an election result that has been deeply shaped by robust Arab turnout.
paras.zh: 该政府现在面临着一种可能性，即它可能会因阿拉伯人强劲投票率而深受影响的选举结果而垮台。

paras.en: Heedo Abu Laban contributed reporting from Lod, Israel.
paras.zh: Heedo Abu Laban 贡献了来自以色列罗德的报道。

paras.en: Days before Tuesday’s pivotal Israeli election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shocked his country by offering a bleak economic forecast that critics said could make Israel more like Iran, Russia and North Korea.
paras.zh: 在周二关键的以色列选举前几天，总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡提出了黯淡的经济预测，批评者称这可能会让以色列变得更像伊朗、俄罗斯和朝鲜，震惊了以色列。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu told an Israeli financial journalist on Friday that he was preparing for international sanctions against Israeli banks by drawing up plans for a “bypass economy” based on cryptocurrency. He also told Israelis to prepare for the end of billions of dollars of annual American assistance.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡周五对以色列财经记者表示，他正在准备制定基于加密货币的“旁路经济”计划，以应对国际社会对以色列银行的制裁。他还告诉以色列人为结束美国每年数十亿美元的援助做好准备。

paras.en: “It’s over,” he said. “It’s only a matter of time.”
paras.zh: “结束了，”他说。 “这只是时间问题。”

paras.en: The comments were a reflection of Israel’s deepening global isolation, with even once-staunch allies imposing or threatening economic sanctions and embargoes after years of war in Gaza and rampant violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
paras.zh: 这些言论反映了以色列日益加深的全球孤立，在加沙多年的战争以及犹太定居者在被占领的约旦河西岸针对巴勒斯坦人的猖獗暴力之后，甚至一度坚定的盟友也实施或威胁实施经济制裁和禁运。

paras.en: With settlers advancing into areas that were previously off limits, Britain last month decried what it called “ethnic cleansing” and announced trade sanctions on settlements that it said would also apply to entities that financed their construction. Though Israel’s banking system has not been directly targeted by sanctions, a dozen countries, including Canada, France and Spain, have said they support restrictions on trade with settlements, raising the prospect of further penalties that could affect Israeli financial institutions.
paras.zh: 随着定居者进入以前禁止进入的地区，英国上个月谴责了所谓的“种族清洗”，并宣布对定居点实施贸易制裁，称这也将适用于为其建设提供资金的实体。尽管以色列的银行系统并未直接成为制裁的目标，但包括加拿大、法国和西班牙在内的十几个国家已表示支持对定居点贸易的限制，这增加了可能影响以色列金融机构的进一步处罚的可能性。

paras.en: Opponents of Mr. Netanyahu’s government decried his pronouncements, which also drew a rebuke from the generally reserved central bank.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡政府的反对者谴责他的言论，这也招致了总体上持保留态度的央行的谴责。

paras.en: “Crypto currencies cannot serve as a route to bypass sanctions against Israel,” the Bank of Israel said in a statement. The bank added that the government would do better “to focus on preventing sanctions” and preserving Israel’s economic ties with its main trading partners.
paras.zh: 以色列央行在一份声明中表示：“加密货币不能成为绕过对以色列制裁的途径。”该银行补充说，政府将更好地“专注于防止制裁”并维护以色列与其主要贸易伙伴的经济联系。

paras.en: Commentators said that Mr. Netanyahu’s outlook sounded apocalyptic, and some said it was part of a scare campaign to improve his election prospects.
paras.zh: 评论人士表示，内塔尼亚胡先生的前景听起来像是世界末日，一些人表示，这是旨在改善他的选举前景的恐吓活动的一部分。

paras.en: Last year, amid growing global condemnation of the Israeli military’s conduct of the war against Hamas in Gaza, where it has been accused of war crimes, and the imposition of some arms embargoes, he warned that Israel would have to become a more self-sufficient “super-Sparta.” That reference to the ancient, insular Greek city-state that practiced militaristic self-reliance was, to critics, a frightening scenario for a small country whose economy is largely driven by a tech sector that is reliant on foreign investment.
paras.zh: 去年，全球越来越多地谴责以色列军队在加沙对哈马斯发动的战争，以色列被指控犯有战争罪，并实施了一些武器禁运，他警告说，以色列必须成为一个更加自给自足的“超级斯巴达”。在批评者看来，对于一个经济主要由依赖外国投资的科技行业驱动的小国来说，希腊这个实行军国主义自力更生的古希腊城邦是一个可怕的场景。

paras.en: Gadi Eisenkot, Mr. Netanyahu’s main rival in Tuesday’s election, said in a social media post that the prime minister’s “Bibi-coin vision,” a nod to cryptocurrency, would “dismantle the Israeli economy for generations.”
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡在周二选举中的主要竞争对手加迪·艾森科特 (Gadi Eisenkot) 在社交媒体帖子中表示，总理的“Bibi-coin 愿景”（对加密货币的认可）将“摧毁以色列几代人的经济”。

paras.en: “No internet purchases, no high-tech investments, no national security,” he added.
paras.zh: “没有互联网购买，没有高科技投资，没有国家安全，”他补充道。

paras.en: Yair Lapid, the opposition leader who has served as prime minister and finance minister, wrote on social media that a vote for Mr. Netanyahu was a vote for “a ruined economy, sanctions that will lead to insane price hikes, and no military alliance with the United States.”
paras.zh: 曾担任总理和财政部长的反对党领袖亚伊尔·拉皮德在社交媒体上写道，投票给内塔尼亚胡先生就是投票给“被破坏的经济、将导致物价疯狂上涨的制裁以及不与美国建立军事联盟”。

paras.en: And a former governor of the Bank of Israel, Jacob Frenkel, told Israel’s Channel 12 on Sunday that moving away from the international financial system would turn Israel into “a leper.”
paras.zh: 以色列银行前行长雅各布·弗伦克尔 (Jacob Frenkel) 周日对以色列第 12 频道表示，脱离国际金融体系将使以色列变成“麻风病人”。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu later walked back his remarks slightly, saying that he had heard the criticism and that cryptocurrency was only one option to deal with potential financial sanctions.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡后来稍微收回了自己的言论，称他听到了批评，加密货币只是应对潜在金融制裁的一种选择。

paras.en: In a somewhat jarring contrast, Mr. Netanyahu’s campaign has argued that Israel’s economy overall is healthy despite years of war, helped by record export revenues, relatively low inflation and unemployment, and a strong shekel.
paras.zh: 与此形成鲜明对比的是，内塔尼亚胡的竞选团队辩称，尽管经历了多年的战争，但得益于创纪录的出口收入、相对较低的通胀和失业率以及坚挺的谢克尔，以色列的经济总体健康。

paras.en: But many Israelis are not feeling it. The State Comptroller, a government watchdog, warned last year that the cost of living was “skyrocketing” in part because of structural challenges in Israel’s consumer market and low competition levels.
paras.zh: 但许多以色列人并没有感觉到。政府监管机构国家审计长去年警告说，生活成本“飙升”，部分原因是以色列消费市场的结构性挑战和低竞争水平。

paras.en: While foreign affairs and national security have dominated the political conversation ahead of the election, a recent survey by the Israel Democracy Institute, a nonpartisan research group, found that the economy was the top issue for many voters heading into Tuesday.
paras.zh: 尽管外交事务和国家安全主导了选举前的政治对话，但无党派研究团体以色列民主研究所最近的一项调查发现，经济是许多选民进入周二的首要问题。

paras.en: The stakes of the Israeli elections are high for Palestinians in the West Bank, but they do not have the right to vote in them.
paras.zh: 对于西岸的巴勒斯坦人来说，以色列选举的赌注很高，但他们没有投票权。

paras.en: In interviews, some Palestinians voiced objections to not being allowed to vote, especially as they felt Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was becoming more permanent.
paras.zh: 在采访中，一些巴勒斯坦人对不被允许投票表示反对，特别是因为他们认为以色列对约旦河西岸的占领正在变得更加永久。

paras.en: “The Israeli government has enormous influence over our lives,” said Montaser Amro, 32, a supermarket owner in Majd, a village near the southern city of Hebron. “It chooses when roadblocks open and close, it controls the borders, and it decides on how much of our economy functions.”
paras.zh: “以色列政府对我们的生活有着巨大的影响力，”32 岁的蒙塔瑟·阿姆罗 (Montaser Amro) 说，他是南部城市希伯伦附近马吉德村的一家超市老板。 “它选择路障何时打开和关闭，它控制边界，并决定我们的经济发挥多少作用。”

paras.en: He added, “Why can’t we vote when settlers living hundreds of meters away can?”
paras.zh: 他补充道，“为什么我们不能投票，而住在数百米外的定居者可以投票？”

paras.en: Israel captured the West Bank in 1967 and reached an agreement with the Palestine Liberation Organization to establish the Palestinian Authority in the 1990s. The Palestinian Authority administers parts of the West Bank and has not held parliamentary or presidential elections for roughly 20 years.
paras.zh: 以色列于1967年占领约旦河西岸，并于20世纪90年代与巴勒斯坦解放组织达成协议建立巴勒斯坦权力机构。巴勒斯坦权力机构管理着约旦河西岸部分地区，大约 20 年没有举行议会或总统选举。

paras.en: Many Palestinians have long hoped the Palestinian Authority would transform into an independent Palestinian state. In recent years, those hopes have dwindled. The Israeli government promotes the expansion of settlements in the West Bank that are widely considered illegal under international law and rejects Palestinian self-determination there and in Gaza. Palestinian officials have also failed to unify their ranks and renew their leadership.
paras.zh: 许多巴勒斯坦人长期以来一直希望巴勒斯坦权力机构能够转变为一个独立的巴勒斯坦国。近年来，这些希望已经越来越渺茫。以色列政府推动在西岸扩建定居点，这些定居点根据国际法被广泛认为是非法的，并拒绝在那里和加沙的巴勒斯坦人自决。巴勒斯坦官员也未能团结他们的队伍并更新他们的领导层。

paras.en: Alaa al-Khabass, 40, a resident of Hebron, said it was unjust that Palestinians could not cast ballots.
paras.zh: 40 岁的希伯伦居民阿拉·哈巴斯 (Alaa al-Khabass) 表示，巴勒斯坦人无法投票是不公正的。

paras.en: “Israel controls just about everything related to us, and I don’t see that changing any time soon,” he said. “We should be able to vote, but we live in painful reality where we lack rights and sovereignty.”
paras.zh: “以色列几乎控制着与我们有关的一切，我认为这种情况不会很快改变，”他说。 “我们应该能够投票，但我们生活在缺乏权利和主权的痛苦现实中。”

articles.title: Israel’s opposition may not be able to form a government, but it still could control Parliament.
articles.author: Isabel Kershner

paras.en: Israel’s political leaders were poised for weeks of negotiations over the shape of the next government, as initial results on Wednesday showed no clear winner in a tightly fought election that many have described as a make-or-break moment for the country.
paras.zh: 以色列政治领导人准备就下届政府的组建进行数周的谈判，周三的初步结果显示，这场激烈的选举没有明显的赢家，许多人称这场选举是该国的成败时刻。

paras.en: If neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hard-line alliance nor an opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot win enough seats to form a government, both would need to find support from outside their blocs for backing as prime minister.
paras.zh: 如果本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理的强硬联盟和加迪·艾森科特领导的反对派集团都无法赢得足够的席位来组建政府，那么双方都需要寻求集团之外的支持来担任总理。

paras.en: By Wednesday evening, election officials had counted about 80 percent of ballots. Those votes, alongside exit polls, indicate that neither bloc would reach the 61 seats needed to secure a straightforward majority in the Knesset, Israel’s Parliament.
paras.zh: 截至周三晚上，选举官员已清点了约 80% 的选票。这些投票以及出口民意调查表明，两个阵营都无法获得在以色列议会中获得绝对多数所需的 61 个席位。

paras.en: Some of Mr. Netanyahu’s allies are floating the idea that he could join Mr. Eisenkot and other centrists to form a broad unity government to stay in power. For Mr. Netanyahu, the long-serving prime minister who remains as a caretaker until a government is formed, that would be a comfortable scenario, as long as he remained on top.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡的一些盟友提出了这样的想法，即他可以与艾森科特和其他中间派一起组建一个广泛的联合政府以继续掌权。对于长期担任总理、在政府组建之前仍担任看守总理的内塔尼亚胡来说，只要他继续掌权，这将是一个舒适的局面。

paras.en: His primary rival, Mr. Eisenkot, faces a dilemma of his own: He has denounced Mr. Netanyahu as unfit to lead Israel, but he has also objected to partnering with Arab parties in a potential coalition. The two Arab parties are projected to win as many as 17 seats — a remarkable show of strength that could make them Mr. Eisenkot’s only path to toppling Mr. Netanyahu.
paras.zh: 他的主要竞争对手艾森科特也面临着自己的困境：他谴责内塔尼亚胡不适合领导以色列，但他也反对与阿拉伯政党合作组建潜在的联盟。预计这两个阿拉伯政党将赢得多达 17 个席位——这是一次非凡的实力展示，可能使它们成为艾森科特推翻内塔尼亚胡的唯一途径。

paras.en: On Wednesday, Mr. Eisenkot did not explicitly mention the Arab parties and instead pledged to build “a stable Zionist government.”
paras.zh: 周三，艾森科特没有明确提及阿拉伯政党，而是承诺建立“一个稳定的犹太复国主义政府”。

paras.en: Most of the votes were expected to be counted by Wednesday, though the final tally could take days. Lengthy negotiations could follow as political parties try to assemble a governing majority. If those talks fail, the country could head to a second round of elections — a scenario that has played out before. For Mr. Netanyahu, running down the clock in the hope of securing a stronger showing in a fresh election could be his strongest shot at retaining his role as prime minister.
paras.zh: 预计大部分选票将在周三清点完毕，但最终统计可能需要几天时间。随着各政党试图聚集执政多数，接下来可能会进行漫长的谈判。如果这些谈判失败，该国可能会进入第二轮选举——这种情况以前已经上演过。对内塔尼亚胡来说，抓紧时间希望在新的选举中获得更好的表现可能是他保住总理职位的最强机会。

paras.en: The uncertainty did not stop the leading candidates from making triumphant late-night speeches to their supporters.
paras.zh: 这种不确定性并没有阻止主要候选人向他们的支持者发表胜利的深夜演讲。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief of staff, struck a defiant tone toward Mr. Netanyahu, saying: “Tonight we got the answer: The public opted for change.”
paras.zh: 以色列前军事参谋长艾森科特对内塔尼亚胡采取了挑衅的语气，他说：“今晚我们得到了答案：公众选择了变革。”

paras.en: A few hours later, Mr. Netanyahu told supporters that his party, Likud, had emerged as the largest in Israel. “We must form a strong right-wing government,” he said.
paras.zh: 几个小时后，内塔尼亚胡先生告诉支持者，他的政党利库德集团已成为以色列最大的政党。 “我们必须组建一个强大的右翼政府，”他说。

paras.en: - More votes: The exit polls do not reflect the hundreds of thousands of votes cast at special polling stations, including at military bases, hospitals, prisons and embassies. In Israel’s 2022 election, those votes tended to favor Mr. Netanyahu and his allies.
paras.zh: - 更多选票：出口民意调查并未反映在军事基地、医院、监狱和大使馆等特殊投票站投下的数十万张选票。在以色列 2022 年的选举中，这些选票往往有利于内塔尼亚胡及其盟友。

paras.en: - Initial results: The 70 percent of the votes counted indicate that Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition will receive about 54 seats, Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc will get roughly 49, and the Arab parties will reach 17. But the numbers could still easily shift.
paras.zh: - 初步结果：70% 的计票结果显示，内塔尼亚胡先生的联盟将获得约 54 个席位，艾森科特先生的集团将获得约 49 个席位，阿拉伯政党将获得 17 个席位。但数字仍可能轻易发生变化。

paras.en: The initial results in the Israeli election released on Wednesday showed that there was no outright winner, and it may take weeks for it to become clear who will be able to form the next government.
paras.zh: 周三公布的以色列选举初步结果显示，没有彻底的获胜者，可能需要数周时间才能清楚谁将能够组建下一届政府。

paras.en: But even if no government is formed, the Israeli Parliament will open on Nov. 10, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s opponents could be well-placed to take control of the legislative process.
paras.zh: 但即使没有组建政府，以色列议会也将于 11 月 10 日开幕，总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡的反对者可能有能力控制立法进程。

paras.en: The Parliament, or Knesset, will open with a swearing in of the 120 lawmakers. Both of the main blocs of Jewish parties likely fell short of winning a majority of seats, and both are reluctant to form a government that relies on a partnership with two predominantly Arab parties.
paras.zh: 议会开幕时，120 名议员将宣誓就职。犹太政党的两个主要集团可能都未能赢得多数席位，而且都不愿意组建一个依赖与两个主要阿拉伯政党合作的政府。

paras.en: But even if the main anti-Netanyahu bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, does not join with Arab parties to form a government, they remain united on some issues. If they join forces in parliamentary votes, they could stymie some of the Netanyahu government’s most contentious policies.
paras.zh: 但即使由加迪·艾森科特领导的主要反内塔尼亚胡集团不与阿拉伯政党一起组建政府，他们在某些问题上仍然保持团结。如果他们在议会投票中联手，可能会阻碍内塔尼亚胡政府一些最具争议的政策。

paras.en: The first requirement would be to choose a new speaker of the house, so that the opposition could take control of the parliamentary agenda, key committees and start enacting laws, experts say.
paras.zh: 专家表示，第一个要求是选择一位新的众议院议长，以便反对派能够控制议会议程、关键委员会并开始颁布法律。

paras.en: “I’m not saying it’s a good scenario to take the Knesset and not be able to form the government,” said Gayil Talshir, a political scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem who is advising the opposition. “It’s a disaster. But this is the hand they are dealt, and they have to play it.”
paras.zh: 为反对派提供咨询的耶路撒冷希伯来大学政治学家盖伊尔·塔尔希尔 (Gayil Talshir) 表示：“我并不是说拿下议会而无法组建政府是一个好局面。” “这是一场灾难。但这就是他们所面临的局面，他们必须打好它。”

paras.en: One of the issues on which Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc and Arab parties agree — beyond wanting to unseat Mr. Netanyahu — is the need for an independent state inquiry into the government’s failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
paras.zh: 艾森科特集团和阿拉伯政党除了希望推翻内塔尼亚胡先生之外，达成一致的问题之一是，需要对政府未能阻止哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日对以色列的袭击进行独立的国家调查。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, who has never taken responsibility for his government’s lapses in failing to stop the attack, has refused to allow such an inquiry. In the new Parliament, the opposition parties could work to establish one.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡从未对其政府未能阻止袭击的失误承担责任，因此拒绝允许进行此类调查。在新议会中，反对党可以努力建立一个议会。

paras.en: Another point that both sides agree on is a desire to overturn laws to carry out a sweeping overhaul of the judiciary.
paras.zh: 双方同意的另一点是希望推翻法律，对司法机构进行全面改革。

paras.en: Supporters of the Netanyahu government’s divisive plan said it was necessary to rein in what they saw as an overactive judiciary, to restore the balance between the branches of government and give more power to elected officials. Critics, however, said the proposed measures would remove checks on government power.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡政府分裂计划的支持者表示，有必要遏制他们认为过度活跃的司法部门，恢复政府各部门之间的平衡，并赋予民选官员更多权力。然而批评者表示，拟议的措施将取消对政府权力的制约。

paras.en: “Damaging legislation and damaging practices were introduced, but they can still be reversed,” said Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute, a nonpartisan research group.
paras.zh: 无党派研究组织以色列民主研究所所长约哈南·普莱斯纳表示：“破坏性的立法和破坏性的做法已经出台，但它们仍然可以逆转。”

paras.en: Other contentious laws that could be challenged include one that politicized the process for appointing Supreme Court judges, and others that weakened the authority of the attorney general and expanded the authority of rabbinical courts.
paras.zh: 其他可能受到质疑的有争议的法律包括一项将最高法院法官任命程序政治化的法律，以及其他削弱总检察长权力并扩大拉比法庭权力的法律。

paras.en: Opposition members have also raised the idea of introducing legislation to bar a candidate charged with a crime from forming a government or to limit a prime minister to two terms in office.
paras.zh: 反对派成员还提出了立法禁止被指控犯罪的候选人组建政府或限制总理连任两届的想法。

paras.en: Both of those efforts would be aimed at Mr. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest serving prime minister who is standing trial on corruption charges.
paras.zh: 这两项努力都将针对以色列任职时间最长的总理内塔尼亚胡，他因腐败指控正在接受审判。

paras.en: But such proposals would be problematic, experts say, because they could be seen as laws targeting Mr. Netanyahu personally and so would likely be challenged in Israel’s Supreme Court.
paras.zh: 但专家表示，此类提议会有问题，因为它们可能被视为针对内塔尼亚胡个人的法律，因此可能会在以色列最高法院受到质疑。

paras.en: Such laws would also not apply retroactively, say, to a candidate who had been indicted in the past, Suzie Navot, an Israeli professor of constitutional law, said.
paras.zh: 以色列宪法学教授苏西·纳沃特表示，此类法律也不会追溯适用于过去被起诉的候选人。

paras.en: “They would not pass easily,” she said. She added the court could postpone such laws so that they could only come into effect in the next Knesset, or even strike them down.
paras.zh: “他们不会轻易通过，”她说。她补充说，法院可以推迟此类法律，以便它们只能在下届议会中生效，甚至推翻它们。

paras.en: David M. Halbfinger contributed reporting.
paras.zh: David M. Halbfinger 贡献了报道。

paras.en: The day after Israel’s election, many supporters of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu felt relief that the results tallied so far showed that the opposition’s path to forming a new government was narrow. Others who had hoped for a decisive opposition victory were crushed by results that could well lead to a political stalemate.
paras.zh: 以色列大选后的第二天，总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的许多支持者感到松了一口气，因为迄今为止的统计结果表明反对派组建新政府的道路狭窄。其他原本希望反对派取得决定性胜利的人却被很可能导致政治僵局的结果压垮了。

paras.en: Almost everyone was asking the same question: What now?
paras.zh: 几乎每个人都在问同样的问题：现在怎么办？

paras.en: “I’m hopeful,” said Merav Katz, 57, a Netanyahu supporter, as she got her hair straightened at a salon in Jaffa. She said she would like to see an all-Jewish unity government with some opposition parties but not including the Arab parties, which made a strong showing.
paras.zh: “我充满希望，”57 岁的内塔尼亚胡支持者梅拉夫·卡茨 (Merav Katz) 在雅法的一家沙龙拉直头发时说道。她说，她希望看到一个全犹太联合政府，其中有一些反对党，但不包括表现强劲的阿拉伯政党。

paras.en: Ms. Katz expressed a sentiment shared by many right-wing voters: An indecisive result among Israeli Jewish voters would put pressure on the opposition to join a coalition with Mr. Netanyahu to avoid another round of elections.
paras.zh: 卡茨女士表达了许多右翼选民的共同看法：以色列犹太选民的优柔寡断的结果将给反对派带来压力，要求他们与内塔尼亚胡先生组成联盟，以避免另一轮选举。

paras.en: The preliminary results show that Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right alliance and the bloc of parties led by Gadi Eisenkot, his main opponent, are both likely to be short of the 61 seats needed to form a majority government.
paras.zh: 初步结果显示，内塔尼亚胡的极右翼联盟及其主要对手加迪·艾森科特领导的政党集团都可能缺乏组建多数政府所需的 61 个席位。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot could extend his hand to the two main Arab parties to form a minority government. Arab citizens, fearing another far-right government, turned out in historically high numbers.
paras.zh: 艾森科特可以向两个主要的阿拉伯政党伸出援手，组建少数派政府。由于担心另一个极右政府，阿拉伯公民参加投票的人数创历史新高。

paras.en: Still, it would be difficult for Mr. Eisenkot, who ran on a center-right campaign, to form an alliance with the largest Arab party, the Joint List, whose leaders often harshly criticize Israel’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，对于以中右翼竞选的艾森科特来说，要与最大的阿拉伯政党“联合名单”结成联盟还是很困难的，该党的领导人经常严厉批评以色列在加沙和约旦河西岸的行动。

paras.en: At the salon in Jaffa, Ms. Katz’s hairdresser, Saado Zorob, 48, an Arab citizen, said that Jewish Israelis seemed happy to be treated by Arab physicians at hospitals and to eat at Arab restaurants but that many were unwilling to give Arab citizens a role in charting the country’s future.
paras.zh: 在雅法的沙龙里，卡茨女士的理发师、48 岁的阿拉伯公民萨多·佐罗布 (Saado Zorob) 表示，犹太以色列人似乎很高兴在医院接受阿拉伯医生的治疗，并在阿拉伯餐馆吃饭，但许多人不愿意让阿拉伯公民在规划国家未来方面发挥作用。

paras.en: “I feel like garbage,” he said as he was blow drying Ms. Katz’s hair. He added that he wished Mr. Eisenkot had the courage to form a government with the Arab caucus. Another election might benefit Mr. Netanyahu. “I’m worried that if the deadlock yields another round of elections, many Arabs will stay home,” he said
paras.zh: “我感觉自己像个垃圾，”他一边吹干卡茨女士的头发一边说道。他补充说，他希望艾森科特先生有勇气与阿拉伯核心小组一起组建政府。另一次选举可能会让内塔尼亚胡先生受益。 “我担心，如果僵局导致新一轮选举，许多阿拉伯人将呆在家里，”他说

paras.en: To many supporters of Mr. Netanyahu, a Jewish-Arab coalition would be a nightmare.
paras.zh: 对于内塔尼亚胡先生的许多支持者来说，犹太-阿拉伯联盟将是一场噩梦。

paras.en: Yakov Matzlawi, 51, a Likud member who manages a men’s undergarment stall in a market in Ramla, near Tel Aviv, said the mood among Netanyahu supporters he knew was subdued. Mr. Netanyahu didn’t lose, he said, but he didn’t win either, and many of on the right were still confused about what the results meant for the country.
paras.zh: 51 岁的利库德集团成员雅科夫·马茨拉维 (Yakov Matzlawi) 在特拉维夫附近的拉姆拉 (Ramla) 的一个市场上经营一个男士内衣摊位，他表示，据他所知，内塔尼亚胡支持者的情绪低迷。内塔尼亚胡先生没有输，他说，但他也没有赢，许多右翼人士仍然对结果对国家意味着什么感到困惑。

paras.en: “What’s important is that we remain in the game,” he said.
paras.zh: “重要的是我们要留在游戏中，”他说。

paras.en: Five miles south, in the city of Rehovot, Shira Barkan, 49, a therapist who wanted to see Mr. Netanyahu’s government fall, sat with her teenage daughter at an açai shop, their bowls only half eaten. “I don’t have much of an appetite,” she said.
paras.zh: 向南 5 英里的雷霍沃特市，49 岁的希拉·巴尔坎 (Shira Barkan) 是一名治疗师，她希望看到内塔尼亚胡政府垮台。她和十几岁的女儿坐在巴西莓店里，他们的碗只吃了一半。 “我没什么胃口，”她说。

paras.en: She had gone to bed the night before hopeful, she said, but “woke up in the morning with Bibi again,” using Mr. Netanyahu’s nickname. In her view, Mr. Netanyahu’s extremist government was leading Israel toward global isolation.
paras.zh: 她说，前一天晚上她满怀希望地入睡，但“早上又和比比一起醒来”，这是内塔尼亚胡先生的昵称。在她看来，内塔尼亚胡先生的极端主义政府正在带领以色列走向全球孤立。

paras.en: “Israelis are amazing people, and they deserve leadership that will not only protect us from external wrongs, but also stop its own wrongdoing,” she said.
paras.zh: 她说：“以色列人是了不起的人民，他们应该得到领导，这不仅能保护我们免受外部错误的侵害，还能制止其自身的错误行为。”

paras.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party is persisting with unproven allegations that Israel’s Arab voters have “stolen the elections.” Israel’s official elections committee has said there was no indication of widespread irregularities in the election on Tuesday. On Wednesday, the Likud again said that Arab parties — which are expected to receive a historically high number of parliamentary seats — had stolen the vote and called for the police and intelligence services to investigate.
paras.zh: 总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团坚持未经证实的指控，称以色列的阿拉伯选民“窃取了选举”。以色列官方选举委员会表示，没有迹象表明周二的选举存在广泛的违规行为。周三，利库德集团再次表示，预计将获得历史最高议会席位的阿拉伯政党窃取了选票，并呼吁警方和情报部门进行调查。

paras.en: Analysts say that Netanyahu is trying to de-legitimize votes by Arab citizens of Israel, fearing that his leading Jewish Israeli opponents might try to link up with the newly empowered Arab political bloc in an effort to unseat him.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，内塔尼亚胡正试图取消以色列阿拉伯公民投票的合法性，担心他的主要犹太以色列反对者可能会试图与新获得权力的阿拉伯政治集团联合起来，试图推翻他。

paras.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel fell short of outright victory on Tuesday night. But he has still emerged with a good chance of clinging to power.
paras.zh: 周二晚上，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡未能取得彻底胜利。但他仍然有很好的机会保住权力。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, 77, has plenty of political blessings to count after the vote. His Likud party is set to remain the largest in the Israeli Parliament, defying the pre-election polls. His rivals, led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot, secured far less support and have been left more divided than expected.
paras.zh: 77 岁的内塔尼亚胡在投票后获得了很多政治上的祝福。他领导的利库德集团将不顾选前民意调查，继续成为以色列议会中最大的政党。由前将军加迪·艾森科特领导的他的竞争对手获得的支持远远少于预期，而且分歧也比预期更大。

paras.en: Analysts say the result, with neither bloc securing enough votes to form a clear majority, could easily lead to weeks or months of political gridlock — a scenario that suits Mr. Netanyahu just fine. He will remain in charge as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed or new elections have to be held.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，结果是，两个阵营都无法获得足够的选票来形成绝对多数，很容易导致数周或数月的政治僵局——这种情况非常适合内塔尼亚胡先生。他将继续担任看守总理，直到新政府组建或必须举行新的选举。

paras.en: It is a remarkable turnaround for Mr. Netanyahu, whose critics blamed him for failing to prevent the Hamas-led attack on Oct. 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israeli history. A consummate political survivor of more than three decades in Israeli politics, Mr. Netanyahu is famous for out-negotiating and manipulating almost every opponent who has tried to end his rule.
paras.zh: 对于内塔尼亚胡先生来说，这是一个显着的转变，他的批评者指责他未能阻止哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日以色列历史上最致命的一天发生的袭击。内塔尼亚胡先生是以色列政坛三十多年的完美政治幸存者，以谈判和操纵几乎所有试图结束其统治的对手而闻名。

paras.en: “Netanyahu is still in the driver’s seat,” said Natan Sachs, an expert on Israeli politics at the Middle East Institute, a Washington-based research group. “He’s still in control of most events, and that’s where he likes to be.”
paras.zh: “内塔尼亚胡仍然占据主导地位，”华盛顿研究机构中东研究所的以色列政治专家纳坦·萨克斯说。 “他仍然控制着大多数事件，这就是他喜欢的地方。”

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, the longest serving prime minister in Israeli history, still has some headaches. The hard-line coalition he formed in 2022 — the most far-right in Israeli history — is set to lose its majority in Israel’s 120-member Parliament.
paras.zh: 以色列历史上任职时间最长的总理内塔尼亚胡仍然面临一些令人头痛的问题。他于 2022 年组建的强硬联盟——以色列历史上最右翼的联盟——将失去以色列 120 名议员议会中的多数席位。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu could also end up losing if Mr. Eisenkot, whose bloc trails the prime minister’s coalition by several seats, chooses to work with the Arab parties that performed better than ever to oust him.
paras.zh: 如果艾森科特选择与表现比以往任何时候都表现更好的阿拉伯政党合作推翻他，内塔尼亚胡最终也可能会失败。艾森科特的阵营落后于总理联盟几个席位。

paras.en: But Mr. Eisenkot is likely to struggle to form such an alliance, given how Israeli public opinion has shifted since the Oct. 7 attacks. Even though Arab leaders in Israel generally condemned the attacks, many Jewish Israelis still regard partnering with them as unacceptable.
paras.zh: 但考虑到自 10 月 7 日袭击以来以色列公众舆论的转变，艾森科特可能很难组建这样的联盟。尽管以色列的阿拉伯领导人普遍谴责这些袭击，但许多犹太以色列人仍然认为与他们合作是不可接受的。

paras.en: “Netanyahu knew he was going to have a weaker bloc. But he knew that his goal, even if he couldn’t get a 61-seat majority, would be to prevent his rivals from forming a government,” said Mazal Mualem, who has written a biography of Mr. Netanyahu. “And it seems he’s succeeded.”
paras.zh: “内塔尼亚胡知道他将拥有一个更弱的集团。但他知道，即使他无法获得 61 个席位的多数席位，他的目标也将是阻止他的竞争对手组建政府，”为内塔尼亚胡先生撰写传记的马扎尔·穆阿利姆 (Mazal Mualem) 说。 “看来他成功了。”

paras.en: All this was hard to imagine just three years ago. Mr. Netanyahu’s public standing plunged after the Oct. 7 attacks, when 1,200 in Israel were killed and 250 were taken hostage, igniting the war in Gaza. Even fervent supporters of the prime minister feared his time in office would end because of his failure to prevent the catastrophe.
paras.zh: 这一切在三年前还是难以想象的。 10 月 7 日的袭击导致以色列 1,200 人死亡、250 人被劫持为人质，并引发了加沙战争，内塔尼亚胡的公众形象一落千丈。即使是总理的狂热支持者也担心他的任期将因他未能阻止这场灾难而结束。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu, however, has tenaciously clambered his way back without accepting any responsibility for the devastating security lapse. Instead, he blamed the assault on Israeli security chiefs, launched a series of military campaigns in Lebanon and Iran that killed some of Israel’s most significant foes, and ran his electoral campaign focused on amplifying fears of Israel’s Arab parties.
paras.zh: 然而，内塔尼亚胡先生顽强地爬回来，没有承担对这一毁灭性安全漏洞的任何责任。相反，他将此次袭击归咎于以色列安全负责人，在黎巴嫩和伊朗发起了一系列军事行动，杀死了以色列的一些最重要的敌人，并在竞选活动中强调了加剧对以色列阿拉伯政党的恐惧。

paras.en: On Tuesday, a swath of Jewish Israelis threw their support behind him, defying Mr. Netanyahu’s critics at home and abroad. The prime minister gave a fiery speech overnight on Wednesday as initial exit polls showed he had outperformed expectations vowing to establish “a patriotic, strong, right-wing government.”
paras.zh: 周二，大批犹太以色列人无视内塔尼亚胡国内外的批评者，支持他。周三晚上，总理发表了激烈的讲话，最初的出口民意调查显示，他的表现超出了预期，誓言要建立“一个爱国、强大的右翼政府”。

paras.en: While a slight shift in the results could upend the electoral map, Mr. Netanyahu has several options for how he might stay in power.
paras.zh: 虽然结果的轻微变化可能会颠覆选举版图，但内塔尼亚胡先生对于如何继续掌权有多种选择。

paras.en: One path would be to try to block any new government from being formed, forcing Israel to hold new elections. Mr. Netanyahu’s opponents — who threw years of energy and planning into the recent vote only to fall short — would struggle to do better in a new vote, analysts say.
paras.zh: 一种途径是试图阻止任何新政府的组建，迫使以色列举行新的选举。分析人士表示，内塔尼亚胡的反对者在最近的投票中投入了多年的精力和计划，但最终未能成功，他们将很难在新的投票中做得更好。

paras.en: “There’s a general sense that this was the opposition’s big chance,” Mr. Sachs said. “From Netanyahu’s perspective, he can throw the dice again and again.”
paras.zh: “人们普遍认为这是反对派的大好机会，”萨克斯说。 “从内塔尼亚胡的角度来看，他可以一次又一次地掷骰子。”

paras.en: Another option would be to form a unity government with one of his opponents. But that will be difficult as long as Mr. Netanyahu insists on staying in the prime minister’s office.
paras.zh: 另一种选择是与他的对手之一组建联合政府。但只要内塔尼亚胡坚持留在总理办公室，这就会很困难。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot has vowed not to serve under Mr. Netanyahu, although a national emergency — such as renewed fighting with Iran — could change that calculation.
paras.zh: 艾森科特发誓不会在内塔尼亚胡手下任职，尽管国家紧急状态——例如与伊朗重新爆发战斗——可能会改变这一想法。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu could also try to pick off potential right-wing defectors from Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc. These include opposition leaders who served in previous Netanyahu governments, such as Naftali Bennett, who leads the center-right Together party, and Avigdor Liberman, who leads the right-wing Yisrael Beitenu.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生还可以尝试从艾森科特先生的集团中剔除潜在的右翼叛逃者。其中包括曾在内塔尼亚胡前任政府任职的反对派领导人，例如领导中右翼团结党的纳夫塔利·贝内特和领导右翼以色列贝特努的阿维格多·利伯曼。

paras.en: Both men are right-wing supporters of Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Both refrained from explicitly endorsing Mr. Eisenkot, Mr. Netanyahu’s main challenger, as the opposition bloc’s candidate for prime minister.
paras.zh: 两人都是以色列占领的约旦河西岸犹太人定居点的右翼支持者。两人都没有明确支持内塔尼亚胡的主要挑战者艾森科特作为反对派集团的总理候选人。

paras.en: But rekindling their old partnerships with Mr. Netanyahu would be difficult. Both Mr. Bennett and Mr. Liberman have considerable bad blood with the prime minister. They have also been strident in demanding an independent commission of inquiry into the failures surrounding the Oct. 7 disaster, which Mr. Netanyahu has resisted.
paras.zh: 但重新点燃与内塔尼亚胡先生的旧有伙伴关系将是困难的。贝内特先生和利伯曼先生都与首相有很大的不和。他们还强烈要求成立一个独立委员会，对 10 月 7 日灾难的失败进行调查，但内塔尼亚胡先生对此表示抵制。

paras.en: Gadi Eisenkot, the leading figure in Israel’s political opposition, had hoped voters would deliver him a clear mandate to form a government, and begin a new era without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the helm.
paras.zh: 以色列政治反对派领袖加迪·艾森科特曾希望选民给予他组建政府的明确授权，并在没有总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡掌舵的情况下开启一个新时代。

paras.en: The initial results show, however, that Mr. Eisenkot and his allies have no easy path to power. They face a dilemma: To secure enough seats in parliament to form a government, they either need to cooperate with Arab-led parties — anathema to many Israelis — or join with Mr. Netanyahu or members of his right-wing alliance.
paras.zh: 然而，初步结果表明，艾森科特及其盟友的掌权之路并不平坦。他们面临着两难境地：为了在议会中获得足够的席位来组建政府，他们要么需要与阿拉伯领导的政党合作（这对许多以色列人来说是一种厌恶），要么与内塔尼亚胡先生或其右翼联盟成员合作。

paras.en: “He’s in a Catch-22,” said Shira Efron, chair of Israel policy at the RAND Corporation. “He doesn’t have a lot of great options.”
paras.zh: “他陷入了第二十二条军规，”兰德公司以色列政策主席希拉·埃夫隆(Shira Efron)说。 “他没有太多好的选择。”

paras.en: If Mr. Eisenkot and the opposition were to join forces with the Arab parties, the results so far suggest that they would need the support of both the major ones: the socially conservative Raam party and the Joint List, a coalition of three factions.
paras.zh: 如果艾森科特先生和反对派要与阿拉伯政党联手，迄今为止的结果表明，他们需要两个主要政党的支持：社会保守派拉姆党和三个派系联盟联合名单党。

paras.en: “After Oct. 7, Israeli society will not accept that,” said Shalom Yerushalmi, a veteran political writer at the news site Zman Yisrael, referring to the 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel. “There’s no chance.”
paras.zh: “10 月 7 日之后，以色列社会将不会接受这一点，”新闻网站 Zman Yisrael 的资深政治作家 Shalom Yerushalmi 表示，他指的是 2023 年哈马斯领导的对以色列南部的袭击。 “没有机会了。”

paras.en: Many Israelis are opposed to any government that would rely on parties that are not Zionist, and would not want those parties to influence security policies or foreign affairs. On the campaign trail, a number of opposition members pledged never to agree to such an arrangement.
paras.zh: 许多以色列人反对任何依赖非犹太复国主义政党的政府，也不希望这些政党影响安全政策或外交事务。在竞选过程中，一些反对派成员承诺永远不会同意这样的安排。

paras.en: Although Raam’s leader, Mansour Abbas, has taken positions more amenable to Zionist members of the opposition, including putting less emphasis on the Palestinian cause, the Joint List has refused to make similar compromises.
paras.zh: 尽管拉姆的领导人曼苏尔·阿巴斯采取了更适合反对派犹太复国主义成员的立场，包括减少对巴勒斯坦事业的重视，但联合名单拒绝做出类似的妥协。

paras.en: In the aftermath of Oct. 7, the leaders of the parties in the Joint List reacted in different ways. Ayman Odeh, who was the head of Hadash, referred to “Hamas’s murderous attack” in an opinion essay for The New York Times. Ahmad Tibi, the leader of Taal, said Arab citizens were against targeting civilians.
paras.zh: 10月7日事件发生后，联合名单各方领导人做出了不同反应。哈达什领导人艾曼·奥德在《纽约时报》的一篇评论文章中提到了“哈马斯的凶残袭击”。塔尔领导人艾哈迈德·提比表示，阿拉伯公民反对针对平民。

paras.en: Sami Abou Shahadeh, the chairman of Balad, said the attack was “an important, historic event in the military sense,” though he later condemned the attack after the Israeli Supreme Court discussed disqualifying him from running for parliament.
paras.zh: 巴拉德主席萨米·阿布·沙哈德表示，这次袭击是“军事意义上的一次重要的历史性事件”，不过在以色列最高法院讨论取消他竞选议会的资格后，他谴责了这次袭击。

paras.en: The prospect of Mr. Eisenkot setting up a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu or members of his bloc appears to be just as challenging. He made Mr. Netanyahu’s record a central theme of his campaign, saying the Israeli prime minister should “go home” and suggesting that he was unfit to lead the country.
paras.zh: 艾森科特与内塔尼亚胡或其集团成员建立联合政府的前景似乎同样具有挑战性。他将内塔尼亚胡的记录作为其竞选活动的中心主题，称以色列总理应该“回家”，并暗示他不适合领导这个国家。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot may be able to come to an agreement with Mr. Netanyahu that excludes some of the most extreme elements of the current Israeli coalition from government — such as the far-right cabinet members Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. But to do so would be to go back on a theme of his campaign.
paras.zh: 艾森科特或许能够与内塔尼亚胡达成协议，将当前以色列联盟中一些最极端的成员排除在政府之外，例如极右翼内阁成员伊塔马尔·本格维尔和贝扎莱尔·斯莫特里奇。但这样做就等于背离了他竞选的主题。

paras.en: “If he goes for a unity government, he would be destroying the whole narrative he has built,” Mr. Yerushalmi said.
paras.zh: “如果他支持联合政府，他就会毁掉他所建立的整个叙事，”耶鲁沙尔米先生说。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot could attempt to convince members of Mr. Netanyahu’s party, Likud, to defect to his side, but that seems unlikely because the long-serving Israeli leader has in the past been highly effective at holding his coalition together.
paras.zh: 艾森科特可能会试图说服内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团成员倒戈到他一边，但这似乎不太可能，因为这位长期任职的以色列领导人过去在维系联盟方面非常有效。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition also includes some ultra-Orthodox parties, which Mr. Eisenkot could try to bring into his bloc. Yet many opposition members are at odds with lawmakers from those parties over the exemptions from military service that many ultra-Orthodox Israelis enjoy.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡的联盟还包括一些极端正统政党，艾森科特可以尝试将这些政党纳入自己的阵营。然而，许多反对派成员与这些政党的立法者在许多极端正统以色列人享有的兵役豁免问题上存在分歧。

paras.en: Another option for Mr. Eisenkot and his partners is to hold out for a new round of elections in the hope of achieving a more favorable result. But that scenario, analysts said, was fraught with pitfalls — Mr. Eisenkot’s supporters, including those living abroad, may be feel less motivated to show up to vote again.
paras.zh: 艾森科特及其伙伴的另一个选择是坚持举行新一轮选举，以期取得更有利的结果。但分析人士表示，这种情况充满了陷阱——艾森科特的支持者，包括那些居住在国外的人，可能会觉得没有动力再次去投票。

paras.en: More than 80 percent of votes have been counted. The initial results continue to suggest that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s alliance nor a bloc of opposition parties led by Gadi Eisenkot is likely to have gained enough seats to form the next government.
paras.zh: 超过80%的选票已经清点完毕。初步结果继续表明，无论是总理内塔尼亚胡的联盟还是加迪·艾森科特领导的反对党集团都不太可能获得足够的席位来组建下一届政府。

paras.en: The results of Israel’s pivotal parliamentary election will not be finalized at least until Thursday and it could be weeks until it is clear what kind of government will be formed and who will lead it. But some conclusions are already inescapable.
paras.zh: 以色列关键的议会选举的结果至少要到周四才能最终确定，可能需要几周时间才能明确将组建什么样的政府以及由谁来领导。但有些结论已经是不可避免的了。

paras.en: Arab citizens of Israel turned out to vote in record numbers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party gobbled up many votes that his right-wing and Orthodox Jewish coalition partners had expected would be theirs. And the pre-election polls failed to anticipate both phenomena.
paras.zh: 以色列的阿拉伯公民参加投票的人数创历史新高。总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团夺取了许多选票，而他的右翼和正统犹太联盟伙伴原以为这些选票会属于他们。选举前的民意调查未能预见到这两种现象。

paras.en: Much could still change. But with most of the votes counted by Wednesday afternoon, here are some initial takeaways.
paras.zh: 很多事情仍然可能发生变化。但由于大部分选票已在周三下午清点完毕，以下是一些初步结论。

paras.en: Netanyahu didn’t win, but Eisenkot lost.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡没有获胜，但艾森科特输了。

paras.en: Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition appears to have shrunk considerably from the 64 parliamentary seats that it won in 2022: The latest results show it with around 54, well short of a majority in the 120-member Knesset, or Parliament. But he could wind up in better position to form a government than his chief rival, Gadi Eisenkot.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生的联盟似乎比 2022 年赢得的 64 个议会席位大幅缩减：最新结果显示，该联盟拥有约 54 个席位，远低于在 120 名议员的议会中获得多数席位。但他最终可能比他的主要竞争对手加迪·艾森科特更有能力组建政府。

paras.en: Mr. Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief of staff, had two goals in the election: to lead the Jewish opposition parties to an outright majority or at least get very close to one, and to make sure his own party, Yashar, got more votes than any other. He failed on both counts, the initial results indicate.
paras.zh: 以色列前军事参谋长艾森科特在选举中有两个目标：带领犹太反对党获得绝对多数或至少非常接近多数，并确保他自己的政党“亚沙尔”获得比其他政党更多的选票。初步结果表明，他在这两方面都失败了。

paras.en: Reuven Hazan, a political science professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said that it had been hard to imagine better conditions for Mr. Eisenkot’s alliance ahead of the election. Mr. Netanyahu and his coalition were weighed down by anger over the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023 attacks and their failure to do more to free Israeli hostages; by anger over ultra-Orthodox Jewish draft-dodging in wartime; and by outrage over the government’s efforts to neuter the judiciary and allow growing settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, he said.
