articles.title: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian refinery raise supply worries

paras.en: Oil prices climbed Wednesday as investors weighed the prospect of a prolonged and widening Middle East conflict after Tehran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's largest refinery.
paras.zh: 德黑兰支持的胡塞武装袭击沙特阿拉伯最大炼油厂后，投资者权衡中东冲突长期且扩大的前景，油价周三上涨。

paras.en: International benchmark Brent crude futures rose $1.50, or 1.32%, to $115.59 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained $1.47, or 1.47%, to $101.37 per barrel.
paras.zh: 国际基准布伦特原油期货上涨1.50美元，涨幅1.32%，至每桶115.59美元；美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨1.47美元，涨幅1.47%，至每桶101.37美元。

paras.en: The Houthis said on Tuesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a ballistic missile, raising worries of an escalation in the regional conflict.
paras.zh: 胡塞武装周二表示，他们用弹道导弹袭击了沙特阿拉伯的拉斯塔努拉炼油厂，引发了人们对地区冲突升级的担忧。

paras.en: Trump, meanwhile, said that the war with Iran would end on his terms, while insisting that Tehran must be prevented from acquiring nuclear weapons.
paras.zh: 与此同时，特朗普表示，与伊朗的战争将按照他的条件结束，同时坚称必须阻止德黑兰获得核武器。

paras.en: Speaking at a campaign rally in Texas on Tuesday, Trump said the conflict could be brought to a swift conclusion but stressed that any agreement must ensure Iran would never possess a nuclear weapon.
paras.zh: 特朗普周二在得克萨斯州的一次竞选集会上发表讲话时表示，冲突可以迅速结束，但强调任何协议都必须确保伊朗永远不会拥有核武器。

paras.en: His remarks followed earlier comments that he was weighing whether to reach a deal with Tehran or pursue further military action, keeping investors on edge over the possibility of renewed strikes.
paras.zh: 此前他曾表示，他正在权衡是否与德黑兰达成协议或采取进一步的军事行动，这让投资者对再次发动袭击的可能性感到紧张。

paras.en: Concerns over disruptions to oil flows have kept a geopolitical risk premium embedded in crude prices, with traders closely monitoring developments in the region.
paras.zh: 对石油流动中断的担忧使得原油价格中蕴藏着地缘政治风险溢价，交易员密切关注该地区的事态发展。

paras.en: Adding to the uncertainty, Israel's election appeared headed for a political stalemate, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, securing a clear path to a governing majority.
paras.zh: 加剧不确定性的是，以色列选举似乎陷入政治僵局，总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡和他的主要挑战者加迪·艾森科特都未能确保获得执政多数席位的明确道路。

paras.en: Preliminary exit polls showed the rival blocs falling short of the 61 seats required to control Israel's 120-member parliament, raising the prospect of protracted coalition negotiations and clouding the outlook for Israel's approach toward Iran.
paras.zh: 初步出口民意调查显示，敌对集团未能达到控制以色列 120 名议员所需的 61 个席位，这增加了旷日持久的联盟谈判的前景，并给以色列对伊朗的态度蒙上了阴影。

articles.title: SK Hynix shares soar over 10 % as profit beats, chipmaker to return $25 billion to investors

paras.en: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix on Wednesday posted a record high quarterly profit, sharply beating estimates, and announced over $25 billion in dividends and buybacks, sending shares more than 10% higher.
paras.zh: 韩国芯片制造商 SK 海力士周三公布季度利润创历史新高，大幅超出预期，并宣布派息和回购超过 250 亿美元，股价上涨逾 10%。

paras.en: Here are SK Hynix's third-quarter results compared with LSEG SmartEstimates, which are weighted toward forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate:
paras.zh: 以下是 SK 海力士第三季度业绩与 LSEG SmartEstimates 的比较，后者根据更一致准确的分析师的预测进行加权：

paras.en: - Revenue: 104.62 trillion won ($78.86 billion) vs. 98.34 trillion won expected
paras.zh: - 收入：104.62万亿韩元（788.6亿美元），预期为98.34万亿韩元

paras.en: - Operating profit: 83.33 trillion won vs. 76.72 trillion won expected
paras.zh: - 营业利润：83.33万亿韩元，预期为76.72万亿韩元

paras.en: Revenue rose 327.9% from a year earlier, while operating profit climbed 632.1% year on year.
paras.zh: 收入同比增长327.9%，营业利润同比增长632.1%。

paras.en: Compared with the previous quarter, revenue climbed 31.9%, while operating profit surged 37.6%.
paras.zh: 与上一季度相比，收入增长31.9%，营业利润增长37.6%。

paras.en: SK Hynix shares rose more than 10%, outperforming the Kospi's 6.25% gain.
paras.zh: SK海力士股价上涨超过10%，跑赢Kospi指数6.25%的涨幅。

paras.en: The company posted record quarterly revenue and operating profit, with sales exceeding 100 trillion won for the first time, as it announced plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders — including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share buybacks and cancellations.
paras.zh: 该公司公布了创纪录的季度收入和营业利润，销售额首次超过100万亿韩元，并宣布计划向股东返还约100万亿韩元，其中包括至少30万亿韩元的现金股息和60万亿韩元的股票回购和注销。

paras.en: In the earnings call, SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung cited financial market volatility and a correction in semiconductor stocks as the main reasons to halt its review of potential pre-IPO fundraising and IPO options for its U.S. subsidiary Solidigm.
paras.zh: 在财报电话会议上，SK 海力士首席执行官 Kwak Noh-Jung 表示，金融市场波动和半导体股票回调是其停止审查其美国子公司 Solidigm 潜在的 IPO 前融资和 IPO 选择的主要原因。

paras.en: The company had said it would continue to assess investment timing, scale and financing options to support Solidigm's growth and enhance shareholder value.
paras.zh: 该公司表示将继续评估投资时机、规模和融资方案，以支持 Solidigm 的增长并提高股东价值。

paras.en: Kwak also outlined plans to return gains from its investment in Japanese chipmaker Kioxia to shareholders, saying that, "We intend to return the gains realized from our investment in Kioxia this year to our shareholders through a special dividend."
paras.zh: 郭还概述了将其对日本芯片制造商 Kioxia 的投资收益返还给股东的计划，并表示：“我们打算通过特别股息将今年对 Kioxia 的投资实现的收益返还给股东。”

paras.en: The chipmaker approved a third-quarter dividend of 14 trillion won, including a special dividend funded by gains from its investment in Kioxia.
paras.zh: 该芯片制造商批准了 14 万亿韩元的第三季度股息，其中包括由其投资 Kioxia 收益资助的特别股息。

paras.en: SK Hynix will also buyback 20 trillion won in shares, half of which will be cancelled this year, after completing its previously announced 40 trillion won shares buyback last week — which will be cancelled shortly — as mentioned in the earnings call.
paras.zh: 正如财报电话会议中提到的，SK海力士上周完成了此前宣布的 40 万亿韩元股票回购计划（即将取消），之后还将回购 20 万亿韩元股票，其中一半将在今年取消。

paras.en: The company also plans to raise its shareholder return target to more than 50% of cumulative free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027, as it expects AI investment momentum to continue due to greater adoption of AI services and a more diverse investor base.
paras.zh: 该公司还计划将其股东回报目标提高到2025年至2027年期间产生的累计自由现金流的50%以上，因为预计由于人工智能服务的更广泛采用和投资者基础更加多元化，人工智能投资势头将持续下去。

paras.en: The company added that it expects the structural supply-demand imbalance in the memory market, where demand outpaces supply, to continue for the time being.
paras.zh: 该公司补充称，预计内存市场的结构性供需失衡现象将暂时持续，供不应求。

paras.en: Mehdi Hosseini, senior equity research analyst at Susquehanna International Group, reiterated his neutral rating on SK Hynix following its third-quarter earnings, saying he preferred Micron and Samsung Electronics over the South Korean chipmaker.
paras.zh: Susquehanna International Group 高级股票研究分析师 Mehdi Hosseini 在 SK 海力士第三季度财报公布后重申了他对 SK 海力士的中性评级，称他更喜欢美光科技和三星电子，而不是这家韩国芯片制造商。

paras.en: He cited Micron's more diversified memory portfolio and Samsung's foundry business as offering a better risk-reward profile.
paras.zh: 他指出，美光科技更加多元化的内存产品组合和三星的代工业务提供了更好的风险回报。

paras.en: Hosseini added that SK Hynix shares were undervalued and that he preferred its U.S.-traded American depositary receipts (ADRs) over its South Korean-listed shares, citing the larger pool of potential investors in the U.S.
paras.zh: Hosseini补充说，SK海力士的股票被低估，他更喜欢在美国交易的美国存托凭证（ADR），而不是在韩国上市的股票，理由是美国有更多的潜在投资者。

paras.en: "I would prefer the ADR in U.S.," he told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia," adding that he was unsure whether there were enough additional buyers in the Korean market.
paras.zh: “我更喜欢美国的 ADR，”他告诉 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Asia”，并补充说他不确定韩国市场是否有足够的额外买家。

paras.en: SK Hynix expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipments and revenue in the fourth quarter, as it ramps up production at its M15X facility in Cheongju, South Korea.
paras.zh: SK 海力士预计，随着韩国清州 M15X 工厂产量的增加，HBM4 在第四季度的出货量和收入将超过 HBM3E。

paras.en: HBM, or high-bandwidth memory, is a type of advanced memory used alongside AI processors to handle large amounts of data. HBM4 is the sixth generation of the technology, which started mass productions and shipments in the third quarter.
paras.zh: HBM（高带宽内存）是一种与 AI 处理器一起使用来处理大量数据的高级内存。 HBM4是该技术的第六代，已于第三季度开始量产出货。

paras.en: Average selling prices for DRAM rose by a high-20s percentage from the previous quarter, driven by higher conventional DRAM prices and a growing share of higher-priced HBM4 sales.
paras.zh: 由于传统 DRAM 价格上涨以及高价 HBM4 销售份额不断增加，DRAM 的平均售价较上一季度上涨了 20% 以上。

paras.en: Meanwhile, shipments of server DDR5 memory chips — a type of memory used in data center servers — rose more than 40% from the previous quarter, as said in the call.
paras.zh: 与此同时，电话会议中表示，服务器 DDR5 内存芯片（数据中心服务器中使用的一种内存）的出货量比上一季度增长了 40% 以上。

paras.en: The company has secured long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50% of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028, expecting memory demand to outpace supply through 2030 and plans to significantly increase investment next year.
paras.zh: 该公司已与14家主要客户签订了长期协议，涵盖2027年和2028年超过50%的产能，预计到2030年内存需求将超过供应，并计划明年大幅增加投资。

articles.title: UBS pre-tax profits jump 27% to $3.59 billion in the third quarter

paras.en: UBS reported a pre-tax profit of almost $3.6 billion in the third quarter, up 27% year on year, largely in line with consensus forecasts.
paras.zh: 瑞银公布第三季度税前利润近36亿美元，同比增长27%，基本符合市场普遍预期。

paras.en: The Swiss banking and asset management giant saw strong net inflows into its global wealth management business.
paras.zh: 这家瑞士银行和资产管理巨头的全球财富管理业务出现了强劲的净流入。

paras.en: Net profits were $2.7 billion for the third quarter, in line with estimates.
paras.zh: 第三季度净利润为 27 亿美元，符合预期。

paras.en: The Zurich-headquartered lender's common equity tier (CET) 1 capital ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — reached 14.7% during the period, up from 14.4% the previous quarter.
paras.zh: 这家总部位于苏黎世的银行的普通股一级资本比率（衡量银行偿付能力的指标）在此期间达到 14.7%，高于上一季度的 14.4%。

paras.en: Strong inflows into its global wealth management business supported performance, with net new assets reaching $55.1 billion by the end of the quarter. UBS recorded $12.5 billion in client commitments across its wealth management and asset management businesses.
paras.zh: 全球财富管理业务的强劲资金流入支撑了业绩，截至本季度末，净新资产达到 551 亿美元。瑞银 (UBS) 的财富管理和资产管理业务的客户承诺额达 125 亿美元。

paras.en: In its third-quarter earnings statement Thursday, the bank said the integration of Credit Suisse is "firmly on track" to be completed by year-end, delivering a total of $13.7 billion in cumulative cost savings, above earlier expectations of $13.5 billion.
paras.zh: 该银行在周四的第三季度收益报告中表示，瑞士信贷的整合“坚定地走在正轨”，将于年底前完成，累计节省成本达 137 亿美元，高于此前预期的 135 亿美元。

articles.title: How a 16th century pirate accidentally spawned a centuries-old math problem

paras.en: Opinions about Sir Walter Raleigh, who sailed the seas in the 16th century, vary widely. Was he a gifted navigator and explorer or a brutal pirate who terrorized the waves? According to one legend, Raleigh was gentlemanly enough to place his cloak in a mud puddle so that Queen Elizabeth I wouldn’t get her feet dirty. But less well known is that with a simple question, he profoundly influenced an area of mathematics that experts still puzzle over today.
paras.zh: 关于 16 世纪航海家沃尔特·罗利爵士 (Sir Walter Raleigh)，人们的看法各不相同。他是一位才华横溢的航海家和探险家，还是一位恐吓海浪的野蛮海盗？根据一个传说，罗利很有绅士风度，将他的斗篷放在泥坑里，这样伊丽莎白女王一世就不会弄脏她的脚。但鲜为人知的是，他通过一个简单的问题对数学领域产生了深远的影响，至今专家们仍然对此感到困惑。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: During his expeditions, Raleigh’s ships carried cannonballs on board for protection against enemy attacks. He wanted to quickly know how many he had at a glance, so he presented his scientific advisor, Thomas Harriot, with a seemingly simple task: calculate the number of cannonballs stacked in a pile. Harriot quickly found a convenient formula for how many were arranged in a square pyramid based on the number in the bottom row and was able to present Raleigh with a satisfactory solution.
paras.zh: 在他的探险期间，罗利的船只携带炮弹以防御敌人的攻击。他想快速知道自己有多少个炮弹，因此他向他的科学顾问托马斯·哈里奥特提出了一个看似简单的任务：计算一堆炮弹的数量。哈里奥特很快就根据底行的数字找到了一个方便的公式，可以计算出四角锥体中的排列数量，并为罗利提供了一个令人满意的解决方案。

paras.en: But Harriot wondered whether that arrangement was truly the densest possible packing of spheres. What if there were an infinite number of cannonballs to consider? In 1606 Harriot wrote a letter to astronomer Johannes Kepler outlining this question. Five years later the scientist published a hypothesis that went down in history as Kepler’s conjecture. To create the densest arrangement of spheres, you start with one sphere in the middle and add six more around it to form a hexagon pattern that can be replicated across an entire plane. A second layer is then formed by nestling the spheres into the resulting spaces like eggs in a carton. The third layer corresponds to the first—and the arrangement continues. Kepler was able to calculate how much free space is created by such stacking: about 26 percent.
paras.zh: 但哈里奥特想知道这种排列是否真的是最密集的球体堆积。如果要考虑无限数量的炮弹怎么办？ 1606 年，哈里奥特给天文学家约翰内斯·开普勒写了一封信，概述了这个问题。五年后，这位科学家发表了一个假设，该假设作为开普勒猜想载入史册。为了创建最密集的球体排列，您可以从中间的一个球体开始，然后在其周围添加六个球体，以形成可以在整个平面上复制的六边形图案。然后，将球体放入所形成的空间中，就像鸡蛋放在纸盒中一样，形成第二层。第三层与第一层相对应——并且这种排列仍在继续。开普勒能够计算出这样的堆叠会产生多少可用空间：大约 26%。

paras.en: It’s worth noting that a finite number of spheres can be arranged much more efficiently; for instance, they can be lined up like a sausage. But Kepler’s problem revolves around an infinite number of spheres in three spatial dimensions. Other configurations Kepler investigated produced larger gaps.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，有限数量的球体可以更有效地排列；例如，它们可以像香肠一样排列起来。但开普勒的问题围绕着三个空间维度中无数个球体。开普勒研究的其他配置产生了更大的间隙。

paras.en: In 1773 physicist and mathematician Joseph Louis Lagrange proved that in two dimensions, the hexagonal configuration is indeed the most space-efficient. It results in a density of about 90 percent, meaning there is only 10 percent empty space. And in 1831 the exceptional mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss was able to prove that Kepler’s conjecture is correct if you assume that the spheres are arranged only in regular lattices. In this case, it is possible to distribute the first few spheres in space and arrange all the others according to the same pattern.
paras.zh: 1773年，物理学家和数学家约瑟夫·路易斯·拉格朗日证明，在二维空间中，六边形结构确实是最节省空间的。它的密度约为 90%，这意味着只有 10% 的空白空间。 1831 年，杰出数学家卡尔·弗里德里希·高斯 (Carl Friedrich Gauss) 能够证明，如果假设球体仅以规则晶格排列，则开普勒猜想是正确的。在这种情况下，可以将前几个球体分布在空间中，并根据相同的图案排列所有其他球体。

paras.en: Gauss could not rule out the possibility of an even denser, more chaotic arrangement, however. This possibility makes the problem considerably more difficult because in this case, every sphere could be placed anywhere—and not just the first few objects. More than a century would pass before the next significant breakthrough.
paras.zh: 然而，高斯不能排除更密集、更混乱的排列的可能性。这种可能性使问题变得更加困难，因为在这种情况下，每个球体都可以放置在任何地方，而不仅仅是前几个对象。一个多世纪之后，下一个重大突破才出现。

paras.en: Because it is impossible to test infinitely many cases, Kepler’s conjecture needed to be reduced to a problem in which only a finite number of configurations are relevant. In 1953 Hungarian mathematician László Fejes Tóth proved that this is indeed possible. The basic idea is to divide three-dimensional space into infinitely many regions and prove that the Kepler configuration is densest in all regions—because then it is also densest in all of space.
paras.zh: 由于不可能测试无限多的情况，因此开普勒猜想需要简化为仅与有限数量的配置相关的问题。 1953 年，匈牙利数学家 László Fejes Tóth 证明这确实是可能的。基本思想是将三维空间划分为无限多个区域，并证明开普勒构形在所有区域中都是最稠密的——因为这样它在所有空间中也是最稠密的。

paras.en: More specifically, Fejes Tóth used a kind of diagram in which he created dots representing the center of the spheres—ensuring each was the diameter of one sphere apart—and then drew boundaries halfway between each point of neighboring points to create a series of separate cells. These so-called Voronoi cells, Fejes Tóth conjectured, must be at least as large in volume as a regular rhombic dodecahedron surrounding a sphere of radius 1. (The rhombic dodecahedron is the shape produced by the most efficient sphere packing in Kepler’s conjecture.) He then considered up to 13 cells and formulated a new problem: if it could be shown that the volume of Voronoi cells is always larger than that of rhombic dodecahedra, then Kepler’s conjecture would be true.
paras.zh: 更具体地说，费杰斯·托特使用了一种图表，其中他创建了代表球体中心的点，确保每个点的直径相隔一个球体，然后在相邻点的每个点之间画出边界，以创建一系列单独的单元。 Fejes Tóth 推测，这些所谓的 Voronoi 单元的体积必须至少与围绕半径为 1 的球体的正菱形十二面体一样大。（菱形十二面体是开普勒猜想中最有效的球体堆积产生的形状。）然后，他考虑了最多 13 个单元，并提出了一个新问题：是否可以证明 Voronoi 单元的体积始终大于菱形的体积十二面体，那么开普勒猜想就成立了。

paras.en: Instead of running through an infinite number of possibilities and checking whether the corresponding packing density is always lower than that proposed by Kepler, Fejes Tóth had proposed a way to examine just a finite number of cases. Even so, the number of arrangements to be tested was enormous—beyond human capabilities alone. It wasn’t until 1992, when American geometer Thomas Callister Hales began working on the problem using a computer, that the effort moved forward. Hales, together with his student Samuel Ferguson, sought a way to work through the numerous cases to prove Kepler’s conjecture, building on Fejes Tóth’s preliminary work. They examined more than 5,000 different arrangements of spheres and showed that their density was lower than that proposed by Kepler, a task that involved approximately 100,000 problems for a computer to solve. The complete implementation took four years.
paras.zh: Fejes Tóth 提出了一种仅检查有限数量情况的方法，而不是遍历无限多种可能性并检查相应的堆积密度是否始终低于开普勒提出的密度。即便如此，需要测试的安排数量还是巨大的——超出了人类的能力。直到 1992 年，美国几何学家托马斯·卡利斯特·黑尔斯 (Thomas Callister Hales) 开始使用计算机研究这个问题时，这项工作才取得了进展。黑尔斯和他的学生塞缪尔·弗格森在费赫斯·托特的前期工作的基础上，寻求一种方法来通过大量案例来证明开普勒猜想。他们检查了 5,000 多种不同的球体排列，结果表明它们的密度低于开普勒提出的密度，而开普勒这项任务需要计算机解决大约 100,000 个问题。完整实施花了四年时间。

paras.en: Hales finally submitted the 250-page proof and three gigabytes of computer files to the prestigious journal Annals of Mathematics in 1998. The reviewers took another four years to examine the proof and concluded that they were 99 percent certain of its correctness.
paras.zh: 黑尔斯最终于 1998 年向著名期刊《数学年鉴》提交了 250 页的证明和 3 GB 的计算机文件。审阅者又花了四年时间检查该证明，并得出结论，他们对其正确性有 99% 的把握。

paras.en: Although this confidence was sufficient for publication in the journal, Hales was still not satisfied. He worried that he might have made a mistake or overlooked a special case. So in 2003 he launched the Flyspeck project (from the acronym FPK, short for Formal Proof of Kepler) to have his calculations checked by a computer-aided proof assistant. It took 11 years to complete that project, but computers fully verified Hales’s work—and found that the proof was correct.
paras.zh: 尽管这种信心足以在期刊上发表，但黑尔斯仍然不满意。他担心自己可能犯了一个错误，或者忽略了一个特殊情况。因此，他在 2003 年启动了 Flyspeck 项目（来自缩写 FPK，开普勒形式证明的缩写），让计算机辅助证明助手检查他的计算结果。该项目花了 11 年时间才完成，但计算机完全验证了黑尔斯的工作，并发现证明是正确的。

paras.en: More than 400 years passed between Sir Raleigh’s original question and the complete solution of the problem. But mysteries remain around dense sphere packing, particularly if you consider the question in higher dimensions. As Henry Cohn, then a mathematician at Microsoft, told Scientific American in 2016: “Part of what I love about the sphere-packing problem is that every dimension has its own idiosyncrasies ... Some dimensions just behave much better than others.”
paras.zh: 从罗利爵士最初提出问题到问题得到彻底解决，已经过去了 400 多年。但围绕致密球体堆积的谜团仍然存在，特别是如果你在更高维度考虑这个问题。正如时任微软数学家亨利·科恩 (Henry Cohn) 2016 年向《科学美国人》表示的那样：“我之所以喜欢球堆积问题，部分原因在于每个维度都有自己的特质……某些维度的表现比其他维度好得多。”

articles.title: OpenAI just scooped human researchers on a million-dollar quantum math problem

paras.en: If you’ve been keeping up with news in the math world, the story will sound strikingly familiar, right down to its cast of characters.
paras.zh: 如果您一直关注数学世界的新闻，这个故事听起来会非常熟悉，甚至包括它的人物阵容。

paras.en: Using a proprietary internal large language model (LLM), OpenAI just released a result mathematicians have been chasing for decades: a formal proof validating the “quantum chromodynamics” that underpin physicists’ best, most successful description of the universe.
paras.zh: OpenAI 使用专有的内部大语言模型 (LLM)，刚刚发布了数学家几十年来一直在追求的结果：验证“量子色动力学”的正式证明，该理论支撑着物理学家对宇宙的最佳、最成功的描述。

paras.en: The new proof also scoops the work of two human mathematicians, one of whom just happens to be employed by OpenAI’s rival Anthropic. The duo—Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge and Ethan Sussman, a mathematician at Northwestern University—had publicly disclosed their progress on their own independent proof in the weeks leading up to OpenAI’s historic announcement.
paras.zh: 新的证明还借鉴了两位人类数学家的工作，其中一位恰好受雇于 OpenAI 的竞争对手 Anthropic。在 OpenAI 历史性宣布之前的几周内，Anthropic 的 Levent Alpöge 和西北大学数学家 Ethan Sussman 两人公开披露了他们在独立证明方面取得的进展。

paras.en: “I’m not going to say that I’m not disappointed,” Sussman says. He and Alpöge first revealed their burgeoning collaboration to the world on October 6. Notably, the pair updated their public GitHub repository with a new set of intermediate results the night before OpenAI’s announcement. “I think we were on the way and maybe even as close as a few weeks away,” Sussman says.
paras.zh: “我不会说我没有失望，”苏斯曼说。他和 Alpöge 于 10 月 6 日首次向全世界透露了他们迅速发展的合作。值得注意的是，两人在 OpenAI 宣布的前一天晚上用一组新的中间结果更新了他们的公共 GitHub 存储库。 “我认为我们已经在路上了，甚至可能还有几周的时间，”萨斯曼说。

paras.en: “This is a major advance,” says Michael R. Douglas, a theoretical physicist and artificial intelligence proponent at Harvard University. “Mathematicians have been trying to make quantum field theory rigorous for over 50 years and have made steady progress, but real-world theories like quantum chromodynamics always seemed out of reach—until now. This is just the start..., but we can hope for rapid progress.”
paras.zh: “这是一个重大进步，”哈佛大学理论物理学家和人工智能支持者迈克尔·R·道格拉斯 (Michael R. Douglas) 说。 “50 多年来，数学家们一直在努力使量子场论变得严格，并取得了稳步进展，但像量子色动力学这样的现实世界理论似乎总是遥不可及——直到现在。这只是一个开始……但我们可以希望取得快速进展。”

paras.en: Both camps were pursuing something known as the Yang-Mills problem, which concerns the math that underpins modern physics. The “Standard Model” of particle physics explains all the known forces in the universe with 17 interacting particles. The particles are described by “quantum fields,” mathematical entities that permeate all of space and time, determining how, when and where particles appear in the world, what they are and what they do.
paras.zh: 两个阵营都在研究所谓的杨-米尔斯问题，该问题涉及支撑现代物理学的数学。粒子物理学的“标准模型”用 17 个相互作用的粒子解释了宇宙中所有已知的力。粒子由“量子场”来描述，量子场是渗透到所有空间和时间的数学实体，决定着粒子如何、何时、何地出现在世界上，它们是什么以及它们做什么。

paras.en: But the math of quantum fields is notoriously gnarly. Physicists use it to reliably predict what happens when they smash particles together at places such as the Large Hadron Collider, but mathematicians worry that the theory has holes.
paras.zh: 但量子场的数学是出了名的粗糙。物理学家用它来可靠地预测当粒子在大型强子对撞机等地方粉碎在一起时会发生什么，但数学家担心该理论存在漏洞。

paras.en: The Yang-Mills problem is about putting that theory on a solid mathematical footing. The problem has two parts: proving that the theory is mathematically consistent—that it “exists”—and proving that it has a nonzero quantity called a “mass gap,” which has important consequences in the physical world.
paras.zh: 杨-米尔斯问题是将这一理论建立在坚实的数学基础上的。这个问题有两个部分：证明该理论在数学上是一致的——它“存在”——并证明它有一个称为“质量间隙”的非零量，这在物理世界中具有重要的影响。

paras.en: In the 1980s mathematician Tadeusz Balaban laid out a coarse path to proving the first part, “existence.” But even just this bare mathematical sketch of a proof was an enormous undertaking, encompassing thousands of pages. And it was far from complete.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代，数学家塔德乌什·巴拉班 (Tadeusz Balaban) 提出了一条粗略的路径来证明第一部分“存在”。但即使只是这个简单的数学证明草图也是一项艰巨的任务，涵盖数千页。而且它还远未完成。

paras.en: “[Balaban’s] papers are not complete and are extraordinarily difficult to read, but experts did not seriously doubt that they could be completed with sufficiently many years devoted to it,” says Roland Bauerschmidt, a mathematician at New York University.
paras.zh: 纽约大学数学家罗兰·鲍尔施密特 (Roland Bauerschmidt) 表示：“[巴拉班]的论文并不完整，而且非常难以阅读，但专家们并不严重怀疑它们可以通过足够多的时间来完成。”

paras.en: Even so, decades have passed, and no other expert has managed to reach the top of the mountain Balaban built—let alone bridge the gaps he left along the way. Balaban himself eventually tired of the project and moved on.
paras.zh: 即便如此，几十年过去了，还没有其他专家能够到达巴拉班建造的山顶，更不用说弥补他沿途留下的空白了。巴拉班本人最终厌倦了这个项目并继续前进。

paras.en: Hopes for progress ramped up only this summer as the rapidly accelerating capabilities of LLMs catapulted them to the forefront of research-level math. In particular, the superhuman endurance of LLMs has let them blast through numerical tedium to persevere where any human would lose interest and give up. Suddenly, an exhausted mathematician could carefully prompt an LLM, get a good night’s sleep and then wake up in the morning to find a completed proof from the tireless, dutiful model.
paras.zh: 直到今年夏天，随着法学硕士能力的迅速提升，将他们推上了研究水平数学的前沿，人们对取得进展的希望才有所增加。特别是，法学硕士的超人耐力让他们能够冲破数字单调的困境，在任何人都会失去兴趣和放弃的地方坚持下去。突然之间，一位疲惫不堪的数学家可以小心翼翼地攻读法学硕士学位，睡个好觉，然后早上醒来，从不知疲倦、尽职尽责的模型中找到完整的证明。

paras.en: Seeing this, Sussman became convinced LLMs were the perfect tool to work on Balaban’s program. “The primary obstacle was the amount of work involved rather than the absence of ideas,” he says. “So from my perspective, this was a rather obvious thing to do.”
paras.zh: 看到这一点，萨斯曼确信法学硕士是从事巴拉班项目的完美工具。 “主要的障碍是所涉及的工作量，而不是缺乏想法，”他说。 “所以从我的角度来看，这是一件相当明显的事情。”

paras.en: At the same time, Alpöge was producing a number of high-profile results with Anthropic’s Claude family of models. In particular, his wrangling of six-dimensional spheres caught Sussman’s attention. “It was the first instance that I had seen of someone being able to get an LLM to produce, reliably, a 100-page proof,” he recalls. That’s the sort of feat that begins to approach the gargantuan tomes typical of Yang-Mills-related work.
paras.zh: 与此同时，Alpöge 借助 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型取得了许多引人注目的成果。特别是，他对六维球体的争论引起了萨斯曼的注意。 “这是我第一次看到有人能够获得法学硕士学位并可靠地提供 100 页的证明，”他回忆道。这是一种开始接近杨米尔斯相关作品中典型的巨著的壮举。

paras.en: So on September 8—which happened to be one of the biggest days in math history—Sussman e-mailed Alpöge. “I essentially told him, ‘Hey, in case no one else has told you, here is something I think would be worth doing,’” he says. Alpöge invited him to collaborate.
paras.zh: 因此，9 月 8 日——这恰好是数学史上最重要的日子之一——Sussman 给 Alpöge 发了电子邮件。 “我基本上告诉他，‘嘿，万一没有人告诉你，我认为这是值得做的事情，’”他说。 Alpöge 邀请他合作。

paras.en: The partnership proceeded much like Alpöge’s work with another mathematician, New York University’s Tristan Buckmaster, on the Euler equations (an important precursor to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, which OpenAI announced it had solved on September 8). Alpöge would use Anthropic’s internal version of Claude—in fact, many “agent” copies of the LLM working in concert—to churn out thousands of pages of mathematical arcana, essentially unreadable to a human. But he’d then use his agents to validate that the arcana corresponded to some real mathematical truth—and to distill it into something easier to parse. He’d then send it to Sussman—who was flabbergasted by how much was borne out by the LLM’s churn.
paras.zh: 此次合作的进展很像 Alpöge 与另一位数学家、纽约大学的特里斯坦·巴克马斯特 (Tristan Buckmaster) 在欧拉方程（纳维-斯托克斯千年奖问题的重要前身，OpenAI 于 9 月 8 日宣布已解决）上的合作。 Alpöge 将使用 Anthropic 的 Claude 内部版本（事实上，LLM 的许多“代理”副本协同工作）来制作数千页的数学奥秘，而这些奥秘对于人类来说基本上是无法阅读的。但随后他会利用他的代理人来验证这个奥秘是否对应于一些真正的数学真理，并将其提炼成更容易解析的东西。然后他将其发送给萨斯曼——法学硕士的流失所证实的程度让萨斯曼大吃一惊。

paras.en: “It’s remarkable,” Sussman says. “The vast majority, if not all, of the mistakes in the version we posted on GitHub were produced by me.”
paras.zh: “这太了不起了，”苏斯曼说。 “我们在 GitHub 上发布的版本中的绝大多数（如果不是全部）错误都是我造成的。”

paras.en: In addition to filling in Balaban’s gaps with a tedious litany of mathematical steps, the agents also made some genuine innovations. “I could tell you exactly how it built on older work,” Sussman says of one example, “but it also was somewhat novel.”
paras.zh: 除了通过一系列繁琐的数学步骤填补巴拉班的空白之外，特工们还做出了一些真正的创新。 “我可以准确地告诉你它是如何建立在旧作品的基础上的，”萨斯曼在谈到一个例子时说道，“但它也有些新颖。”

paras.en: On October 6 Sussman and Alpöge heard the rumors that OpenAI was about to release hundreds of major math results and thought Yang-Mills might be one of them. They decided to proactively start staking their own claim by posting their progress in a public GitHub repository. “I certainly was not the only person to realize this was something worth pursuing,” Sussman says. Their revelation quickly made the rounds on X. Then, when OpenAI’s ensuing “slop drop” didn’t contain a Yang-Mills proof, they continued their work in the open, for all to see.
paras.zh: 10 月 6 日，Sussman 和 Alpöge 听到 OpenAI 即将发布数百项重大数学成果的传言，并认为 Yang-Mills 可能是其中之一。他们决定通过在公共 GitHub 存储库中发布他们的进展来主动开始证明自己的主张。 “我当然不是唯一一个意识到这是值得追求的事情的人，”苏斯曼说。他们的揭露很快在 X 上流传开来。然后，当 OpenAI 随后的“slop drop”不包含 Yang-Mills 证明时，他们继续公开工作，让所有人都看到。

paras.en: After making significant progress this past weekend, the pair updated their repository on Sunday evening. They believed they’d solved the three-dimensional version of the “existence problem.” This would have fallen short of the Clay Mathematical Institute’s Millennium Prize Problem criteria, which demand a four-dimensional solution, but “we expect, based on the ‘slop’ that we have, that the key ideas are the same,” Sussman says.
paras.zh: 在上周末取得重大进展后，两人于周日晚上更新了他们的存储库。他们相信自己已经解决了三维版本的“存在问题”。这可能达不到克莱数学研究所的千年奖问题标准，该标准需要四维解决方案，但“我们预计，根据我们现有的‘坡度’，关键思想是相同的，”苏斯曼说。

paras.en: On Monday evening OpenAI claimed a proof of the “existence” part of the Clay problem. The company has yet to release the proof; instead OpenAI opted to hand it off to a group of experts who could “shepherd” it into the mathematical literature. This decision sparked immediate outcry, including from the advisory group of mathematicians the company itself had assembled in response to earlier backlash.
paras.zh: 周一晚上，OpenAI 声称证明了 Clay 问题的“存在”部分。该公司尚未公布证据；相反，OpenAI 选择将其交给一组专家，他们可以将其“引导”到数学文献中。这一决定立即引发了强烈抗议，其中包括该公司为应对早些时候的强烈反对而组建的数学家顾问小组。

paras.en: Writing on X, Alpöge expressed a mix of disgust and dismay. “I kept telling [Sussman] to not be too deferential and modest because he would be publicly scooped at any opportunity,” Alpöge wrote. “Instead of contacting him to work with him, as has been suggested publicly many times, the people at OpenAI chose to do this.”
paras.zh: Alpöge 在 X 上写道，表达了厌恶和沮丧的情绪。 “我一直告诉[萨斯曼]不要太恭敬和谦虚，因为他会在任何机会被公开报道，”阿尔波格写道。 “OpenAI 的人并没有像多次公开建议的那样联系他并与他合作，而是选择这样做。”

paras.en: In a blog post, OpenAI stated that its internal model—the same one responsible for the Navier-Stokes proof and the subsequent “slop drop”—arrived at the result on September 9. But according to the post, OpenAI opted to keep it secret until the company could code it into Lean, a programming language that helps ensure mathematical correctness. Notably, the OpenAI said this Lean verification took well more than a month, whereas similar checking only took a reported 17 hours for its Navier-Stokes proof.
paras.zh: OpenAI 在一篇博客文章中表示，其内部模型（负责 Navier-Stokes 证明和随后的“slop drop”的模型）于 9 月 9 日得出了结果。但根据这篇文章，OpenAI 选择保守秘密，直到该公司可以将其编码为 Lean（一种有助于确保数学正确性的编程语言）。值得注意的是，OpenAI 表示，这次精益验证花了一个多月的时间，而据报道，其 Navier-Stokes 证明的类似检查只花了 17 个小时。

paras.en: “There is no way it took one month to Lean-verify Yang-Mills,” says Buckmaster, whose very public bout with OpenAI over Navier-Stokes remains largely unresolved. “It takes, at most, a couple of days.”
paras.zh: Buckmaster 表示：“精益验证 Yang-Mills 不可能花费一个月的时间。”Buckmaster 与 OpenAI 就 Navier-Stokes 问题的公开争执基本上仍未解决。 “最多需要几天时间。”

paras.en: As in the Navier-Stokes controversy, this sequence of events shows how impenetrable the provenance of mathematical ideas is becoming. The ongoing rat race between AI companies jockeying for trillion-dollar initial public offering (IPO) valuations continues to come at the cost of scientific clarity and adherence to academic norms. Everyone involved agrees that new norms need to be discussed and established, but no one seems willing to hold back the deluge while that happens.
paras.zh: 正如纳维-斯托克斯争议一样，这一系列事件表明数学思想的起源变得多么难以捉摸。人工智能公司之间为争夺数万亿美元的首次公开募股（IPO）估值而展开的激烈竞争继续以牺牲科学清晰度和遵守学术规范为代价。所有相关人员都同意需要讨论和建立新的规范，但似乎没有人愿意在这种情况发生时阻止洪水泛滥。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (10/27/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（10/27/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory may have just discovered our solar system’s sixth dwarf planet

paras.en: Congratulations to Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake—there may be a new sibling to welcome into the dwarf planet family.
paras.zh: 恭喜冥王星、谷神星、阋神星、豪美亚和鸟神星——矮行星家族可能会迎来一个新的兄弟姐妹。

paras.en: On Tuesday astronomers at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory announced the discovery of a new dwarf planet candidate in a distant part of the solar system beyond Neptune’s orbit. The new object doesn’t have an official name yet and is instead going by its provisional designation—2026 ED138.
paras.zh: 周二，维拉·C·鲁宾天文台的天文学家宣布，在太阳系海王星轨道之外的遥远区域发现了一颗新的候选矮行星。新物体还没有正式名称，而是使用其临时名称 - 2026 ED138。

paras.en: The discovery was made by running billions of pieces of data collected by the Rubin Observatory through a search code developed by Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian astronomers Matthew Holman and Kevin Napier.
paras.zh: 这一发现是通过天体物理中心开发的搜索代码运行鲁宾天文台收集的数十亿条数据而得出的。哈佛和史密森尼天文学家马修·霍尔曼和凯文·纳皮尔。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “My first reaction was one of excited disbelief,” Holman said in a statement. “Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong.”
paras.zh: “我的第一反应是兴奋和难以置信，”霍尔曼在一份声明中说。 “这样的对象非常罕见，所以我立即开始检查我或代码是否做错了。”

paras.en: When Holman and his colleague Mario Jurić of the University of Washington went to double-check, they found 30 more observations of the object by Rubin that dated to between March and July 2026. Looking at other observation tools, the pair found even more sightings going back to 2016. Together, these data allowed the astronomers to begin mapping out 2026 ED138’s orbit.
paras.zh: 当霍尔曼和他华盛顿大学的同事马里奥·尤里奇去仔细检查时，他们发现鲁宾在 2026 年 3 月至 7 月期间对该物体进行了另外 30 次观测。通过查看其他观测工具，两人发现了更多可以追溯到 2016 年的目击事件。总而言之，这些数据使天文学家能够开始绘制 2026 年 ED138 的轨道。

paras.en: The suspected dwarf planet is about 46 times as far from the sun as Earth, making it even more remote than Pluto, which is just 40 times as far. The object is also tilted off the solar system’s plane by around 25 degrees, an arrangement that could be linked to disruptions caused by Neptune’s gravitational pull.
paras.zh: 这颗疑似矮行星距太阳的距离约为地球距太阳的46倍，甚至比冥王星还要遥远，而冥王星的距离仅为地球的40倍。该物体还与太阳系平面倾斜约 25 度，这种排列可能与海王星引力造成的破坏有关。

paras.en: Initial measurements indicate that 2026 ED138 has a diameter between 600 and 1,500 kilometers (373 and 932 miles), which makes it one of the largest dwarf planet candidates yet detected. But size isn’t all that matters: further observations are required to determine if the object has enough mass to be pulled into a round shape, which is a key requirement for a dwarf planet.
paras.zh: 初步测量表明，2026 ED138 的直径在 600 至 1,500 公里（373 至 932 英里）之间，这使其成为迄今为止发现的最大候选矮行星之一。但大小并不是最重要的：需要进一步观察来确定该物体是否有足够的质量来被拉成圆形，这是矮行星的关键要求。

paras.en: Despite its size, 2026 ED138 was able to avoid detection for all these years because it’s located in a part of the night sky that’s crowded with stars whose light drowned it out. The Vera C. Rubin observatory, which is loaded with state-of-the-art, powerful instruments and only recently came online, made the discovery possible. Now that the object has been identified, astronomers can get to work on learning more about it to see if it can join Pluto and the others in the dwarf planet family.
paras.zh: 尽管体积巨大，2026 ED138 多年来仍能避免被发现，因为它位于夜空的一部分，那里挤满了星星，星星的光芒淹没了它。维拉·C·鲁宾天文台配备了最先进、功能强大的仪器，最近才投入使用，使这一发现成为可能。现在这个天体已经被识别出来，天文学家可以开始更多地了解它，看看它是否可以加入冥王星和其他矮行星家族。

paras.en: “If confirmed as a dwarf planet, ED138 would join a very small family of worlds,” Holman said. “Rubin will image the whole southern sky again and again for ten years, so any others hiding in the places earlier surveys skipped are now within reach.”
paras.zh: “如果被确认为矮行星，ED138 将加入一个非常小的世界家族，”霍尔曼说。 “鲁宾将在十年内一次又一次地拍摄整个南方天空，因此任何其他躲藏在先前调查跳过的地方的人现在都触手可及。”

articles.title: Electric stoves could help people with asthma breathe easier
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: For people with asthma, switching from a gas stove to an electric one might be a breath of fresh air. The combustion that creates the flame of a gas stove or oven releases pollutants, including nitrogen dioxide, which can trigger asthma symptoms. After a research-backed electric stove replacement, people reported more symptom relief than is often achieved with asthma medications.
paras.zh: 对于患有哮喘的人来说，从煤气炉换成电炉可能会让人呼吸新鲜空气。燃气灶或烤箱燃烧产生的火焰会释放污染物，包括二氧化氮，这可能引发哮喘症状。在研究支持的电炉更换后，人们报告的症状缓解效果比使用哮喘药物所达到的效果要好。

paras.en: “We were really surprised at how large the benefit was,” says Ashwini Sehgal, a clinician who studies community health at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland. With funding from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency during the Biden administration, Sehgal and colleagues spearheaded a project to install electric stoves in Cleveland households that had at least one person with asthma.
paras.zh: “我们对效果之大感到非常惊讶，”克利夫兰凯斯西储大学研究社区健康的临床医生阿什维尼·塞加尔 (Ashwini Sehgal) 说。在拜登执政期间，在美国环境保护署的资助下，塞加尔和同事牵头了一个项目，为克利夫兰至少有一名哮喘患者的家庭安装电炉。

paras.en: Eighty-five participants who had poorly controlled asthma were given a questionnaire a few months after the switch. They reported symptom improvement that was roughly two to three times as large as what’s typical with medication. Those with the worst symptoms saw the biggest improvement. Participants also reported fewer emergency room or hospital visits and said they missed work or school less often.
paras.zh: 转换后几个月，对 85 名哮喘控制不佳的参与者进行了问卷调查。他们报告说，症状改善程度大约是典型药物治疗的两到三倍。那些症状最严重的人看到了最大的改善。参与者还报告说，去急诊室或医院的次数减少了，并且缺勤或缺课的次数也减少了。

paras.en: One 38-year-old woman told Sehgal’s team that whenever she cooked on her gas stove, she felt like her throat was closing. But the sensation disappeared after she switched to electric. Another participant, a 36-year-old man, found it difficult to walk uphill and play with his kids. With the stove swap, “he described how much better he felt as ‘magical,’ ” Sehgal says.
paras.zh: 一位 38 岁的女性告诉 Sehgal 的团队，每当她在煤气灶上做饭时，她都会感觉喉咙发紧。但当她改用电动后，这种感觉就消失了。另一位参与者是一名 36 岁的男子，他发现很难步行上山并与孩子们玩耍。更换炉灶后，“他形容自己感觉‘神奇’了很多，”塞加尔说。

paras.en: While heating, steaming or frying on a gas stovetop, nearby NO2 levels can skyrocket, reaching hundreds of parts per billion. That’s much higher than the EPA’s one-hour outdoor air quality standard of 100 parts per billion. NO2 exposure is linked to increased asthma symptoms. For example, research in children has found the pollutant can boost wheezing, coughing and asthma attacks.
paras.zh: 在燃气灶上加热、蒸或煎炸时，附近的二氧化氮浓度会飙升，达到十亿分之数百。这远高于 EPA 规定的一小时室外空气质量标准（十亿分之一百）。 NO2 暴露与哮喘症状加重有关。例如，针对儿童的研究发现，污染物会加剧喘息、咳嗽和哮喘发作。

paras.en: The project was initially funded to follow 1,200 households for 12 months. But the Trump administration terminated the EPA’s Community Change Grants early, which drastically reduced the number of study participants. Yet even with this small group, the symptom improvement was significant.
paras.zh: 该项目最初的资助是对 1,200 个家庭进行为期 12 个月的跟踪。但特朗普政府提前终止了美国环保署的社区变革拨款，这大大减少了研究参与者的数量。然而，即使对于这一小群人来说，症状的改善也是显着的。

paras.en: The decision to replace a gas stove “depends on how much you are struggling with your own illness,” says environmental epidemiologist Carrie Breton of WashU Bursky School of Public Health in St. Louis. As a trial run, Sehgal suggests using an electric hot plate and a toaster oven to see if keeping the gas stove off helps improve symptoms.
paras.zh: 圣路易斯华盛顿大学伯斯基公共卫生学院的环境流行病学家卡丽·布雷顿（Carrie Breton）表示，更换燃气灶的决定“取决于你与自己的疾病作斗争的程度”。作为试运行，塞加尔建议使用电热板和烤面包机烤箱，看看关闭燃气灶是否有助于改善症状。

paras.en: If a stove swap isn’t in the budget, reducing NO2 exposure is still worthwhile, says pulmonologist Laura Paulin of Dartmouth Health. She recommends using kitchen ventilation, either via an exhaust hood that vents to the outside or an open window. A HEPA filter with a carbon insert can trap NO2 to decrease airborne concentrations. And try to keep children with asthma out of the kitchen when the stove is on, Paulin says. “It is a daunting task to replace a stove, but it doesn’t have to be an all-or-nothing thing.”
paras.zh: 达特茅斯健康中心的肺病学家劳拉·保林表示，如果预算中没有更换炉灶，减少二氧化氮暴露仍然是值得的。她建议使用厨房通风，可以通过通向室外的排气罩或打开的窗户。带有碳插件的 HEPA 过滤器可以捕获二氧化氮，以降低空气中的浓度。波林说，当炉子打开时，尽量让患有哮喘的孩子远离厨房。 “更换炉子是一项艰巨的任务，但不一定是全有或全无的事情。”

paras.en: For researchers, the next step would be to measure lung function before and after a stove switch, Breton says. It would also be helpful to account for more factors, such as seasonal effects. “Many things can trigger people’s asthma,” Paulin says. Researchers could do a randomized trial in which some people get the electric stove right away while others wait for six months, Sehgal says, to allow time for comparison.
paras.zh: 布雷顿说，对于研究人员来说，下一步将是测量炉灶开关前后的肺功能。考虑更多因素（例如季节性影响）也会有所帮助。 “很多事情都会引发人们的哮喘，”保林说。塞加尔说，研究人员可以进行一项随机试验，其中一些人立即使用电炉，而另一些人则等待六个月，以便有时间进行比较。

paras.en: If electric stoves continue to be linked with fewer trips to the emergency room, fewer hospitalizations and better symptom control than medication can provide, “health insurance companies should consider paying for or subsidizing” stove swaps, Sehgal says. “If it truly works this well,” Breton says, “it’s got a bigger bang for your buck.”
paras.zh: 塞加尔说，如果电炉继续与更少的急诊室次数、更少的住院次数和比药物更好的症状控制联系在一起，“健康保险公司应该考虑支付或补贴”炉灶更换。 “如果它真的运作得这么好，”布雷顿说，“那么你的钱就会得到更大的回报。”

articles.title: Why did humans’ brains surpass chimps’? A tiny foe might help explain it
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: Viruses may be minuscule, but one could have influenced major differences between human and chimpanzee brains.
paras.zh: 病毒可能很小，但一种病毒可能影响人类和黑猩猩大脑之间的重大差异。

paras.en: Millions of years ago, a virus left DNA behind in an African ape’s genome, and the genetic material stuck around in modern day chimps. Those ghosts of infections past appear to influence genes involved in neuron development, which may help explain how human and chimp brains ended up so different, researchers report October 23 in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 数百万年前，一种病毒在非洲猿的基因组中留下了 DNA，而这些遗传物质则留在了现代黑猩猩的体内。研究人员在 10 月 23 日的《科学进展》杂志上报告称，过去的感染痕迹似乎会影响与神经元发育有关的基因，这可能有助于解释人类和黑猩猩的大脑为何会如此不同。

paras.en: Compared with the brains of their chimpanzee kin, human brains are three times larger and more cognitively powerful. Yet “most of their protein-making genes are very similar,” says Johan Jakobsson, a neuroscientist at Lund University in Sweden. In the absence of large differences in the genetic code, Jakobsson and his colleagues decided to look at the parts of the human and chimp genome that control when and where genes are turned on or off.
paras.zh: 与黑猩猩近亲的大脑相比，人类的大脑大三倍，认知能力也更强。然而，“它们的大多数蛋白质制造基因都非常相似，”瑞典隆德大学的神经科学家约翰·雅各布森说。在遗传密码不存在巨大差异的情况下，雅各布森和他的同事决定研究人类和黑猩猩基因组中控制基因开启或关闭的时间和地点的部分。

paras.en: Changes in gene regulation can come from viruses. Some viruses called retroviruses insert their own DNA into their hosts’ genomes to command host cells to build more viruses. But those parasitic bits of DNA can linger long after an infection. If this happens in reproductive cells, the viral DNA gets passed down with the host’s DNA.
paras.zh: 基因调控的变化可能来自病毒。一些称为逆转录病毒的病毒将自己的 DNA 插入宿主的基因组中，以命令宿主细胞构建更多病毒。但这些寄生 DNA 片段在感染后仍会残留很长时间。如果这种情况发生在生殖细胞中，病毒 DNA 就会与宿主的 DNA 一起传递下去。

paras.en: These leftover bits, called endogenous retroviruses, no longer code for the production of infectious viruses, but they can have a big impact on the host’s biology — especially if they make copies of themselves across the genome. And they have. Such viral remnants make up at least 8 percent of the genomes of humans and chimps alike. More generally, these DNA leftovers have been linked with some major evolutionary events, such as the evolution of the mammalian placenta.
paras.zh: 这些残留的片段被称为内源性逆转录病毒，不再编码感染性病毒的产生，但它们可以对宿主的生物学产生重大影响——特别是如果它们在整个基因组中复制自身的话。他们确实做到了。这些病毒残留物至少占人类和黑猩猩基因组的 8%。更一般地说，这些 DNA 残留物与一些重大进化事件有关，例如哺乳动物胎盘的进化。

paras.en: Jakobsson and his colleagues focused on a particular viral vestige in chimps. The holdover came from an infection in an ancestral African ape somewhere between 5 million and 7 million years ago. In chimpanzees, the viral DNA had stuck itself into the genome at 158 different locations. However, it is curiously absent in humans. It’s still unknown why.
paras.zh: 雅各布森和他的同事们专注于黑猩猩身上的一种特殊病毒痕迹。这种残留来自 500 万至 700 万年前非洲猿猴祖先的感染。在黑猩猩中，病毒 DNA 已嵌入基因组的 158 个不同位置。然而，奇怪的是，它在人类中却缺失。目前尚不清楚原因。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to know how that exact pathogen footprint might affect chimpanzees’ brains compared with those of humans. Working with chimpanzee stem cells, they removed the viral DNA using CRISPR, a gene editing technology that allows for precise, targeted cuts in DNA. Once the viral DNA was gone, a nearby gene called LINC00662 — normally silenced in chimpanzees — turned on, making RNA the team could detect. This matches the normal condition in human brain cells, in which LINC00662 is active. The team also used CRISPR to shut off LINC00662 in the human cells, matching the silenced condition seen in chimpanzees.
paras.zh: 研究人员想知道与人类相比，病原体的确切足迹如何影响黑猩猩的大脑。他们利用黑猩猩干细胞，利用 CRISPR 去除了病毒 DNA，这是一种基因编辑技术，可以对 DNA 进行精确、有针对性的切割。一旦病毒 DNA 消失，附近一个名为 LINC00662 的基因（在黑猩猩中通常处于沉默状态）就会开启，产生团队可以检测到的 RNA。这与 LINC00662 处于活跃状态的人脑细胞的正常状态相符。研究小组还使用 CRISPR 关闭人类细胞中的 LINC00662，与黑猩猩中观察到的沉默状态相匹配。

paras.en: When LINC00662 was active in chimp or human cells, the researchers noticed activity boosts to other genes that may be important to brain development — such as genes involved in the development and maturation of neurons and in making new neural connections. It’s not yet clear exactly how the viral DNA’s shutdown of this brain gene network affected the biology of chimpanzee brains. However, this genetic difference may have contributed to a divergence in how human and chimpanzee brains evolved, Jakobsson says. “Our findings show one way an ancient viral [DNA] insertion could create a lasting difference in how a gene is regulated in humans and chimpanzees,” Jakobsson says. Other genetic and environmental changes could be involved in the puzzle as well, he says.
paras.zh: 当 LINC00662 在黑猩猩或人类细胞中活跃时，研究人员注意到其他可能对大脑发育很重要的基因的活性增强，例如参与神经元发育和成熟以及建立新神经连接的基因。目前尚不清楚病毒 DNA 关闭大脑基因网络是如何影响黑猩猩大脑的生物学的。然而，雅各布森说，这种遗传差异可能导致了人类和黑猩猩大脑进化方式的差异。 “我们的研究结果表明，古代病毒 [DNA] 插入可以对人类和黑猩猩的基因调控方式产生持久的差异，”Jakobsson 说。他说，其他遗传和环境变化也可能与这个难题有关。

paras.en: Researchers have previously looked to single letter swaps in DNA to help explain how humans and chimp brains drifted apart in their evolution. But the new study highlights that creatures can rack up genome changes in other ways, says Giorgia Modenini, an evolutionary biologist at the University of Padua in Italy who was not involved with this research.
paras.zh: 研究人员此前曾研究过 DNA 中的单字母交换，以帮助解释人类和黑猩猩的大脑在进化过程中如何渐行渐远。但意大利帕多瓦大学的进化生物学家乔吉亚·莫德尼尼（Giorgia Modenini）表示，这项新研究强调生物可以通过其他方式积累基因组变化，他没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: The researchers do a convincing job of showing that these particular viral leftovers influence developmental differences between human and chimp neurons, says Ravinder Kanda, an evolutionary geneticist at Oxford Brookes University in Oxford, England. “They’ve proved that absolutely. How far that goes, I don’t think we can quite say yet.”
paras.zh: 英国牛津布鲁克斯大学的进化遗传学家 Ravinder Kanda 表示，研究人员做了令人信服的工作，证明这些特殊的病毒残留物会影响人类和黑猩猩神经元之间的发育差异。 “他们已经完全证明了这一点。我认为我们还不能说到底能走多远。”

paras.en: It could be that other controls on genes’ activity are also involved or that this particular ancient lever-puller may represent just a sliver of the viral holdovers that have shaped brain development, Kanda says. “I think there are many, many more retroviruses to be discovered, and at the moment we’ve only touched the tip of the iceberg.”
paras.zh: 坎达说，可能还涉及对基因活动的其他控制，或者这个特殊的古老拉杆器可能只是影响大脑发育的病毒残留物的一小部分。 “我认为还有很多很多的逆转录病毒有待发现，而目前我们只触及了冰山一角。”

articles.title: How brain implants turn thoughts into speech
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Casey Harrell lost his voice to ALS or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. As a volunteer in a clinical trial, he’s helping scientists test a brain-computer interface. Electrode arrays that are implanted in Casey’s brain send signals to nearby computers, where those signals are translated into words he intended to say.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔 (Casey Harrell) 因肌萎缩侧索硬化症 (ALS) 或肌萎缩侧索硬化症而失声。作为临床试验的志愿者，他正在帮助科学家测试脑机接口。植入凯西大脑中的电极阵列向附近的计算机发送信号，这些信号被翻译成他想说的话。

paras.en: Casey uses this system every day to talk with his wife, daughter, friends and work colleagues. The moment he realized that it worked was “pure joy,” Casey says. Even though the researchers scripted his words for that first test, “it was a profound moment,” he says. “The possibilities for the near future for me and the rest of humanity were overwhelming to realize.”
paras.zh: 凯西每天都使用这个系统与他的妻子、女儿、朋友和同事交谈。凯西说，当他意识到它起作用的那一刻，他感到“纯粹的喜悦”。尽管研究人员为第一次测试编写了他的话，但“这是一个意义深远的时刻，”他说。 “对我和其他人来说，不久的将来的可能性是难以想象的。”

paras.en: This episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me follows Casey and the fast-moving neuroscience that enables him to speak.
paras.zh: 这一集《深渊：跟我说话》讲述了凯西和快速发展的神经科学，使他能够说话。

paras.en: Patients paralyzed from the neck down can manipulate robotic arms with their thoughts. The woman in this video is controlling a robot with her mind. The so-called BrainGate system relies on a sensor of electrodes implanted in the motor cortex of the brain. Researchers hope by implanting electrodes in the brain it can read the brain signals meant to move the muscles involved in speaking, and translate the person’s intention to speak into comprehensive speech produced by a computer.
paras.zh: 颈部以下瘫痪的患者可以用意念操纵机械臂。视频中的女人正在用意念控制机器人。所谓的 BrainGate 系统依赖于植入大脑运动皮层的电极传感器。研究人员希望通过在大脑中植入电极，它可以读取大脑信号，从而移动参与说话的肌肉，并将人的说话意图转化为计算机产生的综合语音。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: Controlling things with your mind. It sounds like science fiction, but it’s definitely real. Today, we’re going to explore what it’s like to communicate with a brain implant that decodes your thoughts and turns them into words.
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：用意念控制事物。这听起来像是科幻小说，但它绝对是真实的。今天，我们将探索与大脑植入物进行交流的感觉，该植入物可以解码你的想法并将其转化为语言。

paras.en: [voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? The voice is absolutely an integral part of your identity. Hello? That added layer of it being you. Do you want to talk? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？声音绝对是您身份的一个组成部分。你好？那增加的一层就是你。你想说话吗？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: Sanders: From Science News, I’m Laura Sanders, and this is The Deep End, Talk to Me. Okay, so what is BrainGate? It’s an experimental system that connects electrodes that are implanted in a person’s brain to a nearby computer. It’s called a brain-computer interface, or BCI. The goal here is big: to help people with paralysis or brain injuries or missing limbs regain control over their world.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：来自《科学新闻》，我是劳拉·桑德斯，这里是《深渊》，跟我谈谈。好的，那么 BrainGate 是什么？这是一个实验系统，将植入人大脑的电极连接到附近的计算机。它被称为脑机接口（BCI）。这里的目标很远大：帮助瘫痪、脑损伤或肢体缺失的人重新掌控自己的世界。

paras.en: Leigh Hochberg: BrainGate clinical trials have now been going on for nearly 22 years. It’s 21 point something at the moment.
paras.zh: Leigh Hochberg：BrainGate 临床试验现已进行了近 22 年。现在是 21 点。

paras.en: Sanders: Leigh Hochberg is the director of the BrainGate Consortium and Clinical Trials. He also has a job at Massachusetts General Hospital, Brown University and the VA.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：Leigh Hochberg 是 BrainGate 联盟和临床试验的主管。他还在马萨诸塞州总医院、布朗大学和退伍军人管理局工作。

paras.en: Hochberg: People who may have had a brainstem stroke and suddenly lost the ability both to move and to speak, or for somebody with ALS who is progressively losing the ability to move or to speak, there’s long been a hope that particularly implantable brain-computer interfaces could restore communication and could restore mobility.
paras.zh: Hochberg：对于可能患有脑干中风并突然失去移动和说话能力的人，或者对于逐渐失去移动或说话能力的 ALS 患者，长期以来人们一直希望特别植入的脑机接口可以恢复沟通并恢复活动能力。

paras.en: Sanders: In 2004, a BrainGate device was implanted into a person’s brain for the very first time. That person was a man named Matthew Nagle, and he had been paralyzed in an accident. With BrainGate, he could control a computer cursor with his thoughts. Here’s a 2008 report from IT World.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2004 年，BrainGate 设备首次被植入人的大脑中。那个人名叫马修·内格尔，他在一次事故中瘫痪了。有了 BrainGate，他可以用意念控制电脑光标。这是 IT World 2008 年的报告。

paras.en: Technology gave him hope. He was one of four testing BrainGate, a new technology where a chip is implanted in the brain that picks up electrical impulses. A computer then interprets those impulses as actions.
paras.zh: 科技给了他希望。他是测试 BrainGate 的四人之一，这是一项新技术，将芯片植入大脑中以接收电脉冲。然后计算机将这些冲动解释为动作。

paras.en: Hochberg: Those early studies have been really encouraging, and I think speaks to the potential for the field.
paras.zh: Hochberg：这些早期研究确实令人鼓舞，我认为这说明了该领域的潜力。

paras.en: Sanders: Over the years, there’s been amazing examples of people using BrainGate. People have used it to click around on the internet, play video games, one woman who was paralyzed was even able to drink a cinnamon latte with a robotic arm.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多年来，人们使用 BrainGate 的例子层出不穷。人们用它来上网、玩电子游戏，一位瘫痪的妇女甚至可以用机械臂喝一杯肉桂拿铁。

paras.en: Hochberg: And she was able to think about using her own arm and reach out with a robotic arm and pick up that thermos and bring it to her mouth, and tip it towards her mouth, and then put the straw in her mouth and then to take that sip. And while it wasn’t the first time in nearly 15 years that she had had something to drink, it was the first time that she was really able to do so solely of her own volition. I remember the smile on her face when she did that.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：她能够考虑使用自己的手臂，用机械臂伸出来，拿起保温瓶，将其送到她的嘴边，然后将其朝她的嘴倾斜，然后将吸管放入她的嘴里，然后喝一口。虽然这不是近 15 年来她第一次喝东西，但这是她第一次真正能够完全按照自己的意愿喝东西。我记得她这样做时脸上的笑容。

paras.en: Sanders: Over the decades, BrainGate has had a lot of research success in a lot of ways. But what about talking? Hochberg says that when it comes to decoding speech, the science here is still very, very young.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：几十年来，BrainGate 在很多方面取得了很多研究成功。但是说话呢？霍赫伯格说，在解码语音方面，这门科学还非常非常年轻。

paras.en: Hochberg: We are at early days, just to be super clear. This is the very beginning of this field. There are only a small handful of people in the world who have had any type of implantable BCI that has been decoding speech.
paras.zh: Hochberg：我们还处于早期阶段，需要非常明确。这是这个领域的开始。世界上只有极少数人拥有任何类型的可解码语音的植入式脑机接口。

paras.en: Sanders: Where does the science stand when it comes to decoding the intention to talk? In the past few episodes, we’ve heard the stories of people who have lost their ability to speak. One of those people was Casey Harrell, and Casey also happens to have a BrainGate device implanted in his brain.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在解读谈话意图方面，科学处于什么位置？在过去的几集中，我们听到了失去说话能力的人的故事。其中之一就是凯西·哈雷尔（Casey Harrell），而凯西的大脑中也恰好植入了 BrainGate 设备。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: My name is Casey Harrell and I am 47 years old.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈雷尔：我叫凯西·哈雷尔，今年 47 岁。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey wakes up in the morning, and plugs in.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西早上醒来，然后接通电源。

paras.en: Casey: The first thing I will usually do after getting out of bed is to plug into the Matrix, so to speak.
paras.zh: Casey：可以这么说，我起床后通常要做的第一件事就是插入 Matrix。

paras.en: Sanders: By that, he means attaching two wires to two pedestals that come out of the top of his head. These two black wires then snake down to nearby computers. Collectively, these electrodes in Casey’s brain, wires from his head, and computers are called the BrainGate 2 neural interface system. So Casey gets it all fired up and then he’s off.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的意思是，将两根电线连接到从他头顶伸出的两个基座上。然后这两根黑线蜿蜒连接到附近的计算机。凯西大脑中的这些电极、来自他头部的电线和计算机统称为 BrainGate 2 神经接口系统。所以凯西把一切都点燃了，然后他就出发了。

paras.en: Casey: Unless I have a medical appointment or something that will move me out of the house, I will sit in this position for most of the day, with specifically small breaks in between.
paras.zh: 凯西：除非我有医疗预约或需要离开家的事情，否则我会在一天的大部分时间里保持这个姿势，中间会有特别小的休息时间。

paras.en: Sanders: All the while, Casey is generating brain signals as he thinks about saying words. These are small, precise electrical pulses made by Casey’s neurons, specifically the cells in his speech motor cortex. Remember how we learned there are over 100 muscles that are involved in speech? These are the parts of the brain that control those muscles.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西在思考说话时一直在产生大脑信号。这些是由凯西的神经元（特别是他的言语运动皮层中的细胞）发出的小而精确的电脉冲。还记得我们是如何了解到有超过 100 块肌肉参与言语的吗？这些是控制这些肌肉的大脑部分。

paras.en: Casey: I am using a decoder for about ten to 14 hours a day, seven days a week, for the past almost two years, making me the world’s biggest power user of the brain-to-computer interface known to man.
paras.zh: 凯西：在过去的近两年里，我每周 7 天、每天使用解码器大约 10 到 14 个小时，这使我成为世界上人类已知的脑机接口的最大用户。

paras.en: Sanders: Like Jules, Casey has ALS. The disease has slowly taken away his ability to move and to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：像朱尔斯一样，凯西也患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症。这种疾病慢慢地剥夺了他行动和说话的能力。

paras.en: Casey: I began to lose my ability to talk shortly after my diagnosis in 2020. Then it became a slow motion car crash of multiple years before almost no one would be able to understand me.
paras.zh: 凯西：2020年确诊后不久，我就开始失去说话的能力。然后，这变成了一场长达数年的慢动作车祸，直到几乎没有人能够理解我。

paras.en: By the time of my surgery, only my assistant and my wife, Levana, could really understand me fully. A few other friends who were around often would be able to understand some of what I was saying. I relied upon my assistant and my wife to basically serve as my translators to other people. I did not go anywhere, even a video call without them, either one or both.
paras.zh: 在我接受手术时，只有我的助手和我的妻子莱瓦娜（Levana）能够真正完全理解我。其他一些经常在附近的朋友应该能够理解我在说什么。我基本上依靠我的助手​​和我的妻子充当我向其他人提供翻译的工作。我没有去任何地方，甚至在没有他们的情况下进行视频通话，无论是其中一个还是两个。

paras.en: Sanders: In July of 2023, Casey volunteered for a clinical trial called BrainGate 2. A UC Davis neurosurgeon put four small electrical arrays onto the left side of Casey’s brain. I wanted to know more about how these arrays worked, so I talked to the neurosurgeon who put Casey’s devices into his brain.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2023 年 7 月，凯西自愿参加了一项名为 BrainGate 2 的临床试验。加州大学戴维斯分校的神经外科医生在凯西的左侧大脑上放置了四个小型电子阵列。我想更多地了解这些阵列是如何工作的，所以我与将凯西的设备放入他大脑中的神经外科医生进行了交谈。

paras.en: David Brandman: My name is David Brandman, and I am the co-director of the UC Davis neuroprosthetics lab, developing next-generation neurotechnology to help people with paralysis. A brain-computer interface is a device that records brain signals from people that are paralyzed and then translates those brain signals to allow people to control objects in their environment using their minds.
paras.zh: 大卫·布兰德曼：我叫大卫·布兰德曼，是加州大学戴维斯分校神经修复实验室的联合主任，致力于开发下一代神经技术来帮助瘫痪患者。脑机接口是一种记录瘫痪者大脑信号的设备，然后翻译这些大脑信号，使人们能够用意念控制环境中的物体。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey’s implant is made of four arrays. Each of them are square and they’re about as wide as a peppercorn. Each array has a bunch of pointy ends that go down into his brain. They look a little like those metal cat brushes. Altogether, the four arrays contain 256 electrodes. These electrodes are all listening to Casey’s brain activity when he thinks about saying a word.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西的植入物由四个阵列组成。它们都是方形的，大约有花椒那么宽。每个阵列都有一堆尖头，深入他的大脑。它们看起来有点像那些金属猫刷。四个阵列总共包含 256 个电极。当凯西想要说一句话时，这些电极都会监听他的大脑活动。

paras.en: Brandman: The way this device works is by recording the electrical activity of the brain as he tries to speak.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：这个设备的工作原理是记录他试图说话时大脑的电活动。

paras.en: Sanders: The wires from Casey’s head carry those neural signals to nearby computers. That’s where machine learning algorithms attempt to do a very complex sort of matching. The algorithms match Casey’s brain activity patterns to the patterns that predictably occur with certain sounds called phonemes.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西头部的电线将这些神经信号传送到附近的计算机。这就是机器学习算法尝试进行非常复杂的匹配的地方。这些算法将凯西的大脑活动模式与某些称为音素的声音可预测出现的模式进行匹配。

paras.en: Brandman: We translate his brain signals into one of 39 different English phonemes. Now, a phoneme is a building block of language. So if I say the word hello, the word hello can be broken down into ha, uh, uhl, and oh. Hello.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我们将他的大脑信号翻译成 39 种不同的英语音素之一。现在，音素是语言的组成部分。因此，如果我说“hello”这个词，那么“hello”这个词可以分解为“ha”、“uh”、“uhl”和“oh”。你好。

paras.en: Sanders: Next up, those algorithms assembles these phonemes into words by making its best guess about what Casey wants to say.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：接下来，这些算法通过对凯西想说的话进行最佳猜测，将这些音素组装成单词。

paras.en: Brandman: So I translate this brain activity into a phoneme and then, using artificial intelligence, turn phonemes into words, words into sentences, and sentences into paragraphs.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：所以我将这种大脑活动转化为音素，然后使用人工智能将音素转化为单词，单词转化为句子，句子转化为段落。

paras.en: Sanders: So that’s the process, and it allows Casey to type messages on Slack, text his friends, and send emails. Sometimes in his emails to me, he includes a tagline at the bottom: “Sent from my brain,” with that cute little pink brain emoji. His setup also lets him convert these typed messages into spoken words. These words show up on a screen for him where Casey proofreads them. If everything looks good, Casey gives the go-ahead and the system speaks the words out loud. Brandman tells me that when Casey tries to speak naturally, he can say about six understandable words per minute. That’s pretty slow.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这就是这个过程，它允许凯西在 Slack 上输入消息、给他的朋友发短信以及发送电子邮件。有时，在他给我的电子邮件中，他会在底部添加一个标语：“从我的大脑发送”，并带有可爱的粉红色大脑表情符号。他的设置还可以让他将这些键入的消息转换为口头语言。这些文字出现在他的屏幕上，凯西对其进行校对。如果一切看起来都不错，凯西就会批准，系统就会大声说出这些话。布兰德曼告诉我，当凯西试图自然地说话时，他每分钟可以说大约六个可以理解的单词。那是相当慢的。

paras.en: Brandman: Using this prosthesis, he’s in the ballpark of 50 words per minute. Now, as I’m speaking to you right now, I’m speaking on the order of 120 to 150 words per minute, depending on how excited I am, right? So we’ve got him back to about a third of how quickly he spoke as an able-bodied person.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：使用这个假肢，他大约每分钟可以说 50 个单词。现在，正如我现在对你们讲话一样，我每分钟讲 120 到 150 个单词，具体取决于我的兴奋程度，对吗？因此，我们已经让他恢复了正常人说话速度的三分之一左右。

paras.en: Sanders: I had emailed Casey some questions a few days before our talk. But he didn’t answer them by email. He used his brain-computer interface to answer my questions in real time just by thinking about the words he wanted to say to me. As we introduced ourselves, I saw how the timescale had stretched.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在我们谈话前几天，我通过电子邮件向凯西发送了一些问题。但他没有通过电子邮件回复他们。他通过脑机接口实时回答我的问题，只需思考他想对我说的话。当我们自我介绍时，我发现时间已经被拉长了。

paras.en: Casey: It’s a challenge because we can have this conversation, but I am slower than the average Joe, even where we grew up.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是一个挑战，因为我们可以进行这样的对话，但我比普通人慢，即使在我们长大的地方也是如此。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey and I both grew up in the south, Casey in the Atlanta area and me in middle Tennessee. But he’s lived in the Bay Area for over 20 years now. And like me, his accent had faded.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西和我都在南部长大，凯西在亚特兰大地区，我在田纳西州中部长大。但他已经在湾区生活了 20 多年。和我一样，他的口音也消失了。

paras.en: Casey: And yes, I do not have much of a Southern accent anymore. But I love my roots, and I would love to show my daughter where and how I grew up. But it is exceedingly difficult to travel when you cannot move.
paras.zh: 凯西：是的，我不再有太多南方口音了。但我爱我的根，我很乐意向我的女儿展示我在哪里以及如何长大。但当你无法移动时，旅行就变得非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: Before his mobility was limited, Casey did a lot of cool things.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在行动受限之前，凯西做了很多很酷的事情。

paras.en: Casey: I spent most of my professional career as a climate campaigner and have went all over the globe, fighting companies who are destroying the Earth and trying to bring some justice to our planet and the people who inhabit it. I am very fortunate because I have been able to do something that I love and also develop some deep friendships and relations with other phenomenal people.
paras.zh: 凯西：我职业生涯的大部分时间都是作为气候活动家，并走遍了全球，与破坏地球的公司作斗争，并试图为我们的星球和居住在地球上的人们伸张正义。我很幸运，因为我能够做我喜欢的事情，并与其他杰出的人建立了深厚的友谊和关系。

paras.en: Sanders: My interview with Casey was unlike any I’ve ever had. I’m used to being flexible for interviews. There’s time zone problems, language barriers, mathematicians who sometimes answer my questions in symbols and formulas. But when I logged on to Zoom to talk with Casey, I quickly realized this conversation would be different. I was self-conscious at the beginning of our talk. I fumbled around too much. I’d ask Casey a question and then another one before he had a chance to answer. I accidentally interrupted him a few times. Sometimes I wasn’t sure if he was composing an answer or just waiting for me to say something else. This poor performance on my part wasn’t unusual for Casey at all.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我对凯西的采访与我以往接受过的采访都不一样。 I’m used to being flexible for interviews.有时区问题、语言障碍、数学家有时用符号和公式回答我的问题。但当我登录 Zoom 与凯西交谈时，我很快意识到这次谈话会有所不同。在我们谈话开始时我很不自在。 I fumbled around too much.在凯西有机会回答之前，我会问他一个问题，然后再问另一个问题。 I accidentally interrupted him a few times.有时我不确定他是在写答案还是只是在等我说别的话。我的糟糕表现对凯西来说并不罕见。

paras.en: Casey: It is hard for people in your position to stay focused because you were not used to the cadence of a conversation this slowly.
paras.zh: 凯西：对于你这个职位的人来说，很难保持专注，因为你不习惯如此缓慢的谈话节奏。

paras.en: Sanders: He’s right. I was not used to it. And timing, in conversations and in life, is everything. Here’s Greg Bryant of UCLA.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他是对的。我不习惯。在谈话和生活中，时机就是一切。这是加州大学洛杉矶分校的格雷格·布莱恩特的报道。

paras.en: Bryant: Turns, conversational turns, happen at the level of hundreds of milliseconds at the longest. Two hundred milliseconds is a long turn. That’s a fifth of a second. I mean, that’s really fast. So if you are slow at all, it’s noticeable. We have to coordinate our talk so our terms make sense. I can’t take too long or be too quick to respond to your questions. I have to know when to stop and start. We get into this flow, kind of a dynamic, and that is hugely consequential for how we feel about the conversation, the other person, ourselves. You know, it’s all timing.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：对话，对话的轮转，最长发生在数百毫秒的水平。两百毫秒是一个漫长的转弯。那是五分之一秒。我的意思是，这真的很快。因此，如果你的速度很慢，就会很明显。我们必须协调我们的谈话，以便我们的条款有意义。我不能花太长时间或太快来回答你的问题。我必须知道何时停止和开始。我们进入这种流动状态，一种动态，这对于我们对谈话、对方和我们自己的感受非常重要。你知道，这一切都是时机。

paras.en: Sanders: Let’s turn to Jules. His words start in his brain too, but then they take a different route. He types them by looking at letters on a screen, then his voice clone says them. It’s also a slow process and one that takes a lot of mental power, too. At one point in our conversation, MA describes the effort this requires of Jules.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们来谈谈朱尔斯。他的话语也从他的大脑中开始，但随后却走了不同的路线。他通过查看屏幕上的字母来输入它们，然后他的声音克隆说出它们。这也是一个缓慢的过程，也需要大量的精神力量。在我们的谈话中，MA 描述了 Jules 需要付出的努力。

paras.en: MA: And in his brain, you know, you can imagine he’s doing all these mental gymnastics, to, right now, he’s listening to us. He’s writing something with his eyes, like letter by letter to contribute to the conversation. Plus, he has the answers that he pre-wrote, of the questions that you asked. So it really is like, there’s a whole lot happening behind the scenes that of course anybody who doesn’t have to think about their voice takes for granted. So I’ll pause to let him complete what he’s saying.
paras.zh: MA：在他的大脑中，你知道，你可以想象他正在做所有这些心理体操，现在他正在听我们说话。他正在用眼睛写一些东西，比如一个字母一个字母地写，以促进对话。另外，他还预先写好了您提出的问题的答案。所以，实际上，幕后发生了很多事情，当然，任何不需要考虑自己声音的人都会认为这是理所当然的。所以我会停下来让他完成他所说的。

paras.en: Sanders: MA and I wait here for Jules to weigh in. So far you’ve heard ten seconds of the pause. The full length of the pause was a minute and 18 seconds.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：妈妈和我在这里等朱尔斯发表意见。到目前为止，你已经听到了十秒钟的停顿。整个暂停时间为一分十八秒。

paras.en: Jules: It is a challenge to communicate with people who don’t interact with me on a daily basis. I have a major bottleneck from my thoughts to actually speaking.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：与那些不每天与我互动的人沟通是一个挑战。从我的想法到实际说话，我遇到了一个很大的瓶颈。

paras.en: Sandes: And as with Casey, these pauses can introduce difficulties. Here’s speech pathologist Jessica Pietrowski with more on that.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：和凯西一样，这些停顿可能会带来困难。言语病理学家杰西卡·皮特罗斯基 (Jessica Pietrowski) 对此有更多了解。

paras.en: Pietrowski: Humans are not very comfortable with silence, especially communication. And when we’re talking to one another, we fill in the silences, it’s less awkward. And so, someone who’s communicating with a device is probably very used to those latency periods and some more silence and they’re comfortable with it. Whereas the person they’re communicating with is like, let’s keep it going, like this is, I want to help, I want to fill in the blanks, I don’t want this to feel awkward, but in turn, might make it a little more awkward than they think.
paras.zh: Pietrowski：人类不太适应沉默，尤其是交流。当我们互相交谈时，我们会填补沉默，这样就不那么尴尬了。因此，与设备通信的人可能非常习惯这些等待时间和更多的沉默，他们对此感到很舒服。而与他们交流的人却说，让我们继续下去，就像这样，我想提供帮助，我想填补空白，我不想让这感觉尴尬，但反过来，可能会让事情比他们想象的更尴尬。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules hates when people read his screen before he’s ready to say what he wants. This particular hate inspired a joke in his stand-up routine.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯讨厌人们在他准备好说出他想说的话之前阅读他的屏幕。这种特殊的仇恨在他的脱口秀节目中引发了一个笑话。

paras.en: [Jules audio]: People read off my screen while I’m typing and try to finish what I am saying. It’s like having to constantly deal with an over-competitive charades partner.
paras.zh: [Jules 音频]：当我打字时，人们会从我的屏幕上读出内容，并尝试完成我所说的内容。这就像必须不断地与竞争过度的猜字游戏伙伴打交道。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules and Casey encounter other people’s impatience constantly. Not that it isn’t well-intentioned but still, it does not help. Even worse, they face other people’s misconceptions about what they’re capable of. Casey is an interesting, funny and compelling conversationalist. That might not be apparent to everyone who doesn’t slow down to hear him. And that’s an assumption that really bothers him.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯和凯西经常遇到其他人的不耐烦。并不是说它不是出于好意，但它仍然没有帮助。更糟糕的是，他们面临着其他人对他们能力的误解。凯西是一位有趣、风趣且引人注目的健谈者。对于那些不放慢速度听他讲话的人来说，这一点可能并不明显。这个假设确实让他困扰。

paras.en: Casey: It is incredibly undignified and a terrible consequence of the health care system to treat me like this very quickly.
paras.zh: 凯西：医疗保健系统如此迅速地对待我，这是非常不尊严的，也是一个可怕的后果。

paras.en: Sanders: Brandman has seen this dismissal, this mistreatment too. It happens with some of the volunteers he works with on the BrainGate 2 project I mentioned earlier. That’s the same trial Casey’s in.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：布兰德曼也看到过这种解雇和虐待。我之前提到的与他一起参与 BrainGate 2 项目的一些志愿者身上就发生过这种情况。这与凯西所参加的审判相同。

paras.en: Brandman: I think as healthcare professionals, we conflate the inability to communicate with the lack of understanding. And I’ve witnessed this firsthand as I’ve watched doctors and nurses interact with my BrainGate participants and then treat them as if they are invalid. Or they’re not there because they’re unable to express themselves. And in fact, I go out of my way in the intensive care unit on the wards and dealing with anyone who’s dealing with my participants to say, look, you know, they’re inside. They’re there. They can understand everything that’s happening. They just happen to not be able to speak. And so please treat them with the respect and dignity that they deserve. And it’s a constant challenge for the participants that I work with. And it’s the reality of which we face and it’s the bias that we have against people that can’t speak for themselves.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我认为作为医疗保健专业人员，我们将无法沟通与缺乏理解混为一谈。我亲眼目睹了这一点，因为我看到医生和护士与我的 BrainGate 参与者互动，然后像对待病人一样对待他们。或者他们不在那里是因为他们无法表达自己。事实上，我在病房的重症监护室里不遗余力地对待任何与我的参与者打交道的人，说，看，你知道，他们在里面。他们就在那里。他们可以理解正在发生的一切。他们只是碰巧无法说话。因此，请给予他们应有的尊重和尊严。对于与我一起工作的参与者来说，这是一个持续的挑战。这就是我们面临的现实，这就是我们对那些不能为自己说话的人的偏见。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey and the other people with ALS are not alone. Many people who have trouble talking or who just need more time can be judged this way. Here’s Karina Nagin from Bridging Voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西和其他患有 ALS 的人并不孤单。许多说话有困难或者只是需要更多时间的人都可以这样判断。这是来自 Bridging Voice 的卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 的报道。

paras.en: Nagin: It’s how people see you. And so when you have ALS and you cannot move and you don’t even have facial expressions and you’re hooked up to machines, people assume you’re not there. And we see this every day where people either don’t talk to the person with ALS, assuming that they can’t respond. They speak really loudly and slow. Their mind is completely working.
paras.zh: 纳金：这就是人们如何看待你。因此，当你患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）时，你无法移动，甚至没有面部表情，而且你还连接着机器，人们会认为你不在那里。我们每天都会看到这样的情况：人们要么不与 ALS 患者交谈，认为他们无法做出回应。他们说话声音很大而且很慢。他们的头脑完全运转。

paras.en: Sanders: For now, Casey’s words may be slow. But despite all the drawbacks, they are still an absolute marvel. Remember Hochberg from the start of this episode? He’s one of the neuroscientists who works with Casey, and he told me a story from the first few days of testing after Casey’s BCI was implanted.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：目前来看，凯西的话可能会很慢。但尽管有这些缺点，它们仍然是一个绝对的奇迹。还记得本集一开始的霍赫伯格吗？他是与凯西一起工作的神经科学家之一，他给我讲了凯西脑机接口植入后最初几天测试的故事。

paras.en: Hochberg: We gave him a 50-word vocabulary on day one. And even on day one, he was able to say some key sentences from those 50 high-value words.
paras.zh: Hochberg：第一天我们就给了他 50 个单词的词汇。即使在第一天，他就能说出这 50 个高价值单词中的一些关键句子。

paras.en: Sanders: At this point in the testing, Casey was asked to say some pre-specified sentences so researchers could test their system out.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在测试的这个阶段，凯西被要求说出一些预先指定的句子，以便研究人员可以测试他们的系统。

paras.en: Casey: Most of the sentences were what we called closed loops.
paras.zh: 凯西：大多数句子都是我们所说的闭环。

paras.en: Sanders: That means that the researchers already knew what brain activity patterns should go with the words Casey thought about saying. It was a test to see if the system was working.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这意味着研究人员已经知道什么大脑活动模式应该与凯西想要说的话相匹配。这是一个测试，看看系统是否正常工作。

paras.en: Casey: The decoder would be able to verify whether I was right or wrong, giving me short preloaded sentences to say. I was asked to say, “What good is that?”
paras.zh: 凯西：解码器将能够验证我是对还是错，给我预先加载的简短句子。我被要求说：“那有什么好处？”

paras.en: Sanders: “What good is that?” is not the most poignant sentence ever uttered, but it had a big effect both in the room and for researchers joining remotely by video.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：“那有什么好处？”这并不是有史以来最令人心酸的一句话，但它在房间里和通过视频远程加入的研究人员中产生了很大的影响。

paras.en: Casey: “What good is that?” Everyone is crying after I am successful.
paras.zh: 凯西：“那有什么好处？”当我成功后，每个人都在哭泣。

paras.en: Sanders: Later on, there was time for Casey to actually express himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：后来凯西有时间真正表达自己的想法。

paras.en: Casey: It was only after the first few sessions that I had any real time to say what I wanted for a good amount of time in relative privacy. That said, it was pure joy, even though I wasn’t getting to say what I wanted to say in that moment. It was a profound moment for me. The possibilities for the near future, for me and the rest of humanity were overwhelming to realize.
paras.zh: 凯西：只有在最初的几次会议之后，我才有时间在相对私密的情况下在相当长的时间内说出我想要的内容。也就是说，这是纯粹的快乐，尽管我当时没能说出我想说的话。这对我来说是一个意义深远的时刻。对于我和其他人来说，不久的将来的可能性是难以想象的。

paras.en: Sanders: Things only got better from there. To set the scene here, during this session, Hochberg was in his office and Casey was at his home, sitting in his living room. Hochberg was watching Casey on a screen.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从那时起事情只会变得更好。为了设置这里的场景，在这次会议期间，霍赫伯格在他的办公室里，凯西在他的家里，坐在他的客厅里。霍赫伯格正在屏幕上看着凯西。

paras.en: Hochberg: On the second session, came back and gave him the full 125,000 plus word English dictionary to be able to select from. That is, the decoders and the AI and the machine learning language models would be able to select from basically a full dictionary. And the first thing that he said was something along the lines of, “Is this thing on?” Kind of a funny statement.
paras.zh: Hochberg：在第二次会议上，回来后给了他完整的 125,000 多个单词的英语词典供他选择。也就是说，解码器、人工智能和机器学习语言模型将能够从基本上完整的字典中进行选择。他说的第一句话是这样的：“这个东西开着吗？”有点有趣的说法。

paras.en: The next thing that he said on the second day of using brain-computer interface, or the second thing that we decoded was, “I’m looking for a cheetah.” And it’s the second day. We know there’s all kinds of opportunities for decoding errors. And when I saw that, I said, you know, there’s no way that the second sentence on the second day of using an implanted brain-computer interface is going to say anything about a cheetah. You know, that’s obviously a decoding error and that’s fine.
paras.zh: 使用脑机接口的第二天，他说的下一句话，或者说我们解码的第二件事是，“我在寻找猎豹。”而且已经是第二天了。我们知道存在各种解码错误的机会。当我看到这一点时，我说，你知道，使用植入脑机接口的第二天的第二句话不可能说任何关于猎豹的事情。你知道，这显然是一个解码错误，但没关系。

paras.en: Sanders: Hochberg could see Casey on the screen, but he couldn’t see something really important that had just happened in the room.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：霍赫伯格可以在屏幕上看到凯西，但他看不到房间里刚刚发生的真正重要的事情。

paras.en: Hochberg: His four-year-old daughter had just walked into the room dressed as a cheetah.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：他四岁的女儿刚刚打扮成猎豹走进房间。

paras.en: Sanders: Here’s Casey remembering the same moment.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是凯西回忆起的同一时刻。

paras.en: Casey: Yes, I remember this time very well. It was the second session of talking that I experienced early in August 2024. My daughter was incredibly cute in her cheetah outfit. This was one of her favorite animals. They were going through a phase where everything they did was super fast, running from thing to thing. Everyone was thinking that it must have been a mistake that I could not use this language. It was so random. This was only from the people like Leigh who were not in the room with us. The researchers who were there could validate that, yes, I said this. I meant it because of the unique context.
paras.zh: 凯西：是的，这一次我记得很清楚。这是我在 2024 年 8 月上旬经历的第二次谈话。我女儿穿着猎豹装，非常可爱。这是她最喜欢的动物之一。他们正在经历一个阶段，他们所做的一切都非常快，从一件事跑到另一件事。每个人都认为我不会使用这种语言一定是一个错误。真是太随意了。这只是来自像 Leigh 这样的人，他们没有和我们一起在房间里。那里的研究人员可以证实，是的，我说过这一点。我这么说是因为独特的背景。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s one of those moments that many parents have. A kid does something cute, a parent plays along. But in this moment for Casey and his child, it was anything but ordinary.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是许多父母都会经历的时刻之一。孩子做一些可爱的事情，父母也跟着一起玩。但此刻对于凯西和他的孩子来说，这绝非平常。

paras.en: Hochberg: And she was born around the time that he was diagnosed with ALS. And one could imagine that because the voice that was coming out of the computer was a version of his own voice, and then the rest of the interaction was between dad and daughter. And it was between parent and child.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：她是在他被诊断出患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症的时候出生的。人们可以想象，因为从电脑中传出的声音是他自己声音的一个版本，然后剩下的互动就发生在爸爸和女儿之间。而且是父母和孩子之间的事。

paras.en: Sanders: The BCI had given Casey something priceless, a minute to play with his sweet little cheetah.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：BCI 给了凯西一些无价的东西，那就是和他可爱的小猎豹玩耍的一分钟。

paras.en: Casey: I was quietly confident that it would work the way it ended up working for me. I had done a lot of research and the thing was that the technology was on the cusp of a breakthrough. And why not me? I asked myself.
paras.zh: 凯西：我暗自相信它会以最终为我工作的方式发挥作用。我做了很多研究，事实是这项技术正处于突破的边缘。为什么不是我呢？我问自己。

paras.en: Sanders: Early on in the research project, Casey and his wife had been told not to expect it to work. This was an experiment and the outcome was far from certain. Casey, however, was optimistic.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在研究项目的早期，凯西和他的妻子被告知不要指望它会起作用。这是一个实验，结果还远未确定。然而，凯西却很乐观。

paras.en: Hochberg: So to me, seeing it work that quickly and that powerfully really, really emphasized that these are technologies that are going to be able to restore not only activities of daily living, not only key kind of instrumental activities of daily living, but they’re going to restore communication between parent and child. They’re going to restore communication between friends and family and care partners and health care providers.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：所以对我来说，看到它如此迅速和强大地发挥作用，确实强调了这些技术不仅能够恢复日常生活活动，不仅能够恢复日常生活的关键工具性活动，而且它们还将恢复父母和孩子之间的沟通。他们将恢复朋友、家人、护理伙伴和医疗保健提供者之间的沟通。

paras.en: Sanders: Because this is a podcast about the human voice, I’ve been asking people I interview what their voice means to them. Here’s Casey’s answer.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：因为这是一个关于人类声音的播客，所以我一直在问我采访的人他们的声音对他们意味着什么。这是凯西的回答。

paras.en: Casey: It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：这意义重大。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: Getting it back, even in a limited form, is everything.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：收回它，即使是以有限的形式，也是一切。

paras.en: Casey: It was so amazing to be able to be understood right from the get-go and to be able to talk and respond, respond to my daughter, especially because that was lacking completely from my life up to that point.
paras.zh: 凯西：能够从一开始就被理解，能够与我的女儿交谈和回应，回应我的女儿，这真是太神奇了，特别是因为在那之前我的生活完全缺乏这一点。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey’s restored voice changed his life.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西恢复的声音改变了他的生活。
